af.label: Name origin
af.text: The name "Afghan" originally referred to the Pashtun people, but today it is understood to include all the country's ethnic groups; the suffix "-stan" means "place of" or "country," so Afghanistan literally means the "Land of the Afghans".

af.label: National anthem
af.text: The national anthem of Afghanistan is "Milli Surood" (National Anthem).

af.label: National symbol
af.text: Afghanistan's national symbol is the lion.

af.label: Independence
af.text: Afghanistan became independent from UK control over Afghan foreign affairs on 19 August 1919.

af.label: World Heritage
af.text: Afghanistan has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Minaret of Jam and Buddhas of Bamyan.

af.label: Highest point
af.text: The highest point in Afghanistan is Noshak, at 7,492 m.

al.label: Name origin
al.text: Name may be derived from the pre-Celtic word alb, meaning "hill," or from the Indo-European root word albh, meaning "white;" the local name "Shqiperia" is derived from the Albanian word shqiponje ("eagle") and is popularly interpreted to…

al.label: National anthem
al.text: The national anthem of Albania is "Hymni i Flamurit" (Hymn to the Flag). Only the first two stanzas of the original poem are used, with the second stanza as a chorus.

al.label: National symbol
al.text: Albania's national symbol is the black double-headed eagle.

al.label: Independence
al.text: Albania became independent from the Ottoman Empire on 28 November 1912.

al.label: World Heritage
al.text: Albania has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Butrint and Historic Berat and Gjirokastër.

al.label: Highest point
al.text: The highest point in Albania is Maja e Korabit (Golem Korab), at 2,764 m.

dz.label: Name origin
dz.text: The country name derives from the capital city of Algiers.

dz.label: National anthem
dz.text: The national anthem of Algeria is "Kassaman" (We Pledge). Zakariah wrote "Kassaman" as a poem while imprisoned in Algiers by French colonial forces.

dz.label: Independence
dz.text: Algeria became independent from France on 5 July 1962.

dz.label: World Heritage
dz.text: Algeria has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Beni Hammad Fort and Djémila.

dz.label: Highest point
dz.text: The highest point in Algeria is Tahat, at 2,908 m.

dz.label: Population
dz.text: About 48 million people live in Algeria.

ad.label: Name origin
ad.text: The origin of the country's name is obscure; may originate from the Navarrese word andurrial, meaning "shrub-covered land;" alternatively, may derive from the Arabic ad-darra meaning "the forest," a reference to its location.

ad.label: National anthem
ad.text: The national anthem of Andorra is "El Gran Carlemany" (The Great Charlemagne). The anthem provides a brief history of Andorra in a first-person narrative.

ad.label: National symbol
ad.text: Andorra's national symbol is the red cow (breed unspecified).

ad.label: World Heritage
ad.text: Andorra has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley.

ad.label: Highest point
ad.text: The highest point in Andorra is Pic de Coma Pedrosa, at 2,946 m.

ao.label: Name origin
ao.text: In the 15th century, Portuguese explorers derived the name from the title "N'gola," which was held by kings of the Ndongo.

ao.label: National anthem
ao.text: The national anthem of Angola is "Angola Avante" (Forward Angola).

ao.label: National symbol
ao.text: Angola's national symbol is the giant black sable antelope (Palanca negra gigante).

ao.label: Independence
ao.text: Angola became independent from Portugal on 11 November 1975.

ao.label: World Heritage
ao.text: Angola has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Mbanza-Kongo.

ao.label: Highest point
ao.text: The highest point in Angola is Moco, at 2,620 m.

ag.label: Name origin
ag.text: Antiguo is Spanish for "ancient" or "old;" Christopher Columbus named the island in 1493, after the church of Santa Maria la Antigua (Old Saint Mary's) in Seville, Spain.

ag.label: National anthem
ag.text: The national anthem of Antigua and Barbuda is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

ag.label: National symbol
ag.text: Antigua and Barbuda's national symbol is the fallow deer.

ag.label: Independence
ag.text: Antigua and Barbuda became independent from the UK on 1 November 1981.

ag.label: World Heritage
ag.text: Antigua and Barbuda has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Antigua Naval Dockyard (Nelson's Dockyard).

ag.label: Highest point
ag.text: The highest point in Antigua and Barbuda is Mount Obama, at 402 m.

ar.label: Name origin
ar.text: The name is derived from one of the Spanish words for "silver," but the origin is unclear; it may have described the land next to the Rio de la Plata ("Silver River"), a major river that forms the boundary between Argentina and Uruguay.

ar.label: National anthem
ar.text: The national anthem of Argentina is "Himno Nacional Argentino" (Argentine National Anthem). Vicente Lopez was inspired to write the anthem after watching a play about the 1810 May Revolution against Spain.

ar.label: National symbol
ar.text: Argentina's national symbol is the Sun of May (a sun-with-face symbol).

ar.label: Independence
ar.text: Argentina became independent from Spain on 9 July 1816.

ar.label: World Heritage
ar.text: Argentina has 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Los Glaciares National Park and Jesuit Missions of the Guaranis.

ar.label: Highest point
ar.text: The highest point in Argentina is Cerro Aconcagua (located in the northwestern corner of the province of Mendoza; highest point in South America), at 6,962 m.

am.label: Name origin
am.text: The etymology of the country's name remains obscure; according to tradition, the local name for the country, Hayastan, comes from Hayk, the legendary patriarch of the Armenians and the great-great-grandson of Noah.

am.label: National anthem
am.text: The national anthem of Armenia is "Mer Hayrenik" (Our Fatherland). Based on the anthem of the Democratic Republic of Armenia (1918-1922), but with different lyrics.

am.label: National symbol
am.text: Armenia's national symbols are the Mount Ararat, eagle and lion.

am.label: World Heritage
am.text: Armenia has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Monasteries of Haghpat and Sanahin and Monastery of Geghard and the Upper Azat Valley.

am.label: Highest point
am.text: The highest point in Armenia is Aragats Lerrnagagat', at 4,090 m.

am.label: Population
am.text: About 3 million people live in Armenia.

au.label: Name origin
au.text: The name Australia derives from the Latin australis meaning "southern;" the Australian landmass was long referred to as "Terra Australis," or the Southern Land.

au.label: National anthem
au.text: The national anthem of Australia is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

au.label: National symbol
au.text: Australia's national symbols are the Commonwealth Star (seven-pointed Star of Federation), golden wattle tree (Acacia pycnantha), kangaroo and emu.

au.label: Independence
au.text: Australia became independent from the federation of UK colonies on 1 January 1901.

au.label: World Heritage
au.text: Australia has 21 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Great Barrier Reef and Greater Blue Mountains Area.

au.label: Highest point
au.text: The highest point in Australia is Mount Kosciuszko, at 2,228 m.

at.label: Name origin
at.text: The name Oesterreich means "eastern realm" and dates to the 10th century; the designation refers to the fact that Austria was the easternmost extension of Bavaria and the German peoples; the word Austria is a Latinization of the German name.

at.label: National anthem
at.text: The national anthem of Austria is "Bundeshymne" (Federal Hymn).

at.label: National symbol
at.text: Austria's national symbols are the eagle, edelweiss and Alpine gentian.

at.label: World Heritage
at.text: Austria has 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Salzburg and Palace and Gardens of Schönbrunn.

at.label: Highest point
at.text: The highest point in Austria is Grossglockner, at 3,798 m.

at.label: Population
at.text: About 9.2 million people live in Austria.

az.label: Name origin
az.text: The name can be translated as "Fire Keeper" or "The Land of Fire," from the local word azer, or "fire," and baydjan, a word derived from the Iranian word baykan, or "guardian;" may refer to fire worshippers who lived in the region.

az.label: National anthem
az.text: The national anthem of Azerbaijan is "Azerbaijan Marsi" (March of Azerbaijan). Originally written in 1919 during a brief period of independence, but did not become the official anthem until after the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

az.label: National symbol
az.text: Azerbaijan's national symbol is the flames of fire.

az.label: World Heritage
az.text: Azerbaijan has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Walled City of Baku and Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape.

az.label: Highest point
az.text: The highest point in Azerbaijan is Bazarduzu Dagi, at 4,466 m.

az.label: Population
az.text: About 11 million people live in Azerbaijan.

bs.label: Name origin
bs.text: Name may be derived from the Spanish baha mar, meaning "low sea," which describes the shallow waters of the Bahama Banks; alternatively, it may be a form of the local name Guanahani, which is of unknown origin and meaning.

bs.label: National anthem
bs.text: The national anthem of the Bahamas is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

bs.label: National symbol
bs.text: The Bahamas' national symbols are the blue marlin, flamingo and yellow elderflower.

bs.label: Independence
bs.text: The Bahamas became independent from the UK on 10 July 1973.

bs.label: Highest point
bs.text: The highest point in the Bahamas is 1.3 km NE of Old Bight on Cat Island, at 64 m.

bs.label: Population
bs.text: About 415,000 people live in the Bahamas.

bh.label: Name origin
bh.text: The name means "the two seas" in Arabic and refers to the water bodies on each side of the archipelago.

bh.label: National anthem
bh.text: The national anthem of Bahrain is "Bahrainona" (Our Bahrain). Mohamed Sudqi Ayyash wrote the original lyrics, but they were changed in 2002 after Bahrain became a kingdom.

bh.label: National symbol
bh.text: Bahrain's national symbol is the a white serrated band with five white points on top of a red field.

bh.label: Independence
bh.text: Bahrain became independent from the UK on 15 August 1971.

bh.label: World Heritage
bh.text: Bahrain has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Dilmun Burial Mounds and Qal'at al-Bahrain – Ancient Harbor and Capital of Dilmun.

bh.label: Highest point
bh.text: The highest point in Bahrain is Jabal ad Dukhan, at 135 m.

bd.label: Name origin
bd.text: The name is a compound of the Bengali words Bangla (Bengali) and desh (country).

bd.label: National anthem
bd.text: The national anthem of Bangladesh is "Amar Shonar Bangla" (My Golden Bengal). Rabindranath Tagore, a Nobel laureate, also wrote India's national anthem.

bd.label: National symbol
bd.text: Bangladesh's national symbols are the Bengal tiger and water lily.

bd.label: Independence
bd.text: Bangladesh became independent from Pakistan on 16 December 1971.

bd.label: World Heritage
bd.text: Bangladesh has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Bagerhat Historic Mosque and Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur.

bd.label: Highest point
bd.text: The highest point in Bangladesh is Mowdok Taung, at 1,060 m.

bb.label: Name origin
bb.text: The name is the plural of the Spanish word barbado and means "the bearded ones," which could refer either to the beard-like leaves of the island's fig trees or to the beards of Carib inhabitants.

bb.label: National anthem
bb.text: The national anthem of Barbados is "The National Anthem of Barbados".

bb.label: National symbol
bb.text: Barbados' national symbols are the Neptune's trident, pelican and red bird of paradise flower (also known as "Pride of Barbados").

bb.label: Independence
bb.text: Barbados became independent from the UK on 30 November 1966.

bb.label: World Heritage
bb.text: Barbados has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison.

bb.label: Highest point
bb.text: The highest point in Barbados is Mount Hillaby, at 336 m.

by.label: Name origin
by.text: The name is a compound of the Slavic words "bel" (white) and "Rus" (the Old East Slavic ethnic designation) to form the meaning White Rusian or White Ruthenian.

by.label: National anthem
by.text: The national anthem of Belarus is "My, Bielarusy" (We Belarusians). After the fall of the Soviet Union, Belarus kept the music of its Soviet-era anthem but adopted new lyrics.

by.label: Independence
by.text: Belarus became independent from the Soviet Union on 25 August 1991.

by.label: World Heritage
by.text: Belarus has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Białowieża Forest and Mir Castle Complex.

by.label: Highest point
by.text: The highest point in Belarus is Dzyarzhynskaya Hara, at 346 m.

by.label: Population
by.text: About 9.5 million people live in Belarus.

be.label: Name origin
be.text: The name derives from the Belgae, an ancient Celtic tribal confederation that inhabited an area between the English Channel and the west bank of the Rhine in the first centuries B.C.

be.label: National anthem
be.text: The national anthem of Belgium is "La Brabançonne" (The Song of Brabant).

be.label: National symbol
be.text: Belgium's national symbol is the golden rampant lion.

be.label: World Heritage
be.text: Belgium has 16 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Belfries of Belgium and Historic Brugge.

be.label: Highest point
be.text: The highest point in Belgium is Botrange, at 694 m.

be.label: Population
be.text: About 12 million people live in Belgium.

bz.label: Name origin
bz.text: Traditionally believed to be derived from the Spanish pronunciation of the last name of Scottish explorer Peter Wallace, who settled in the area in 1638.

bz.label: National anthem
bz.text: The national anthem of Belize is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

bz.label: National symbol
bz.text: Belize's national symbols are the Baird's tapir (a large forest-dwelling mammal), keel-billed toucan and black orchid.

bz.label: Independence
bz.text: Belize became independent from the UK on 21 September 1981.

bz.label: World Heritage
bz.text: Belize has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System.

bz.label: Highest point
bz.text: The highest point in Belize is Doyle's Delight, at 1,124 m.

bj.label: Name origin
bj.text: The current name comes from a local ethnic group, the Bini, whose name may be related to the Arabic word bani, meaning "sons;" the former name, Dahomey, comes from a previous kingdom in the area called Dan Homé.

bj.label: National anthem
bj.text: The national anthem of Benin is "L'Aube Nouvelle" (The Dawn of a New Day).

bj.label: National symbol
bj.text: Benin's national symbol is the leopard.

bj.label: Independence
bj.text: Benin became independent from France on 1 August 1960.

bj.label: World Heritage
bj.text: Benin has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Royal Palaces of Abomey and W-Arly-Pendjari Complex.

bj.label: Population
bj.text: About 15 million people live in Benin.

bt.label: Name origin
bt.text: Name may derive from the Sanskrit words bhoṭa, the name for Tibet, and anta, meaning "end" -- a reference to Bhutan's location at the southernmost end of Tibet; the local Dzongkha name Druk Yul means "Land of the Dragon".

bt.label: National anthem
bt.text: The national anthem of Bhutan is "Druk tsendhen" (The Thunder Dragon Kingdom).

bt.label: National symbol
bt.text: Bhutan's national symbol is the mythical thunder dragon (druk).

bt.label: Highest point
bt.text: The highest point in Bhutan is Gangkar Puensum, at 7,570 m.

bt.label: Capital
bt.text: The capital of Bhutan is Thimphu.

bo.label: Name origin
bo.text: The country is named in honor of Simón Bolívar, a 19th-century leader in the South American wars for independence.

bo.label: National anthem
bo.text: The national anthem of Bolivia is "Cancion Patriotica" (Patriotic Song).

bo.label: Independence
bo.text: Bolivia became independent from Spain on 6 August 1825.

bo.label: World Heritage
bo.text: Bolivia has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including City of Potosi and El Fuerte de Samaipata.

bo.label: Highest point
bo.text: The highest point in Bolivia is Nevado Sajama, at 6,542 m.

bo.label: Population
bo.text: About 12 million people live in Bolivia.

ba.label: Name origin
ba.text: The larger northern territory is named for the Bosna River; the smaller southern section takes its name from the Old Serbian word herceg, meaning "duke," combined with the possessive -ov and the suffix -ina, meaning "country," to denote…

ba.label: National anthem
ba.text: The national anthem of Bosnia and Herzegovina is "Drzavna himna Bosne i Hercegovine" (The National Anthem of Bosnia and Herzegovina).

ba.label: National symbol
ba.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina's national symbol is the golden lily.

ba.label: Independence
ba.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina became independent from Yugoslavia on 1 March 1992.

ba.label: World Heritage
ba.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Old Bridge Area of Mostar and Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge in Višegrad.

ba.label: Highest point
ba.text: The highest point in Bosnia and Herzegovina is Maglic, at 2,386 m.

bw.label: Name origin
bw.text: The name Botswana means "Land of the Tswana," referring to the country's largest ethnic group.

bw.label: National anthem
bw.text: The national anthem of Botswana is "Fatshe leno la rona" (Our Land).

bw.label: National symbol
bw.text: Botswana's national symbol is the zebra.

bw.label: Independence
bw.text: Botswana became independent from the UK on 30 September 1966.

bw.label: World Heritage
bw.text: Botswana has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Tsodilo Hills and Okavango Delta.

bw.label: Highest point
bw.text: The highest point in Botswana is Manyelanong Hill, at 1,495 m.

br.label: Name origin
br.text: The country name derives from the brazil tree that used to grow plentifully along the coast of Brazil and that was used to produce a deep red dye.

br.label: National anthem
br.text: The national anthem of Brazil is "Hino Nacional Brasileiro" (Brazilian National Anthem). The anthem's music, composed in 1822, was used unofficially for many years.

br.label: National symbol
br.text: Brazil's national symbol is the Southern Cross constellation.

br.label: Independence
br.text: Brazil became independent from Portugal on 7 September 1822.

br.label: World Heritage
br.text: Brazil has 24 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Brasilia and Historic Salvador de Bahia.

br.label: Highest point
br.text: The highest point in Brazil is Pico da Neblina, at 2,994 m.

bn.label: Name origin
bn.text: Derivation of the name is unclear; the name may come from the Sanskrit word bhumi, meaning "land" or "region".

bn.label: National anthem
bn.text: The national anthem of Brunei is "Allah Peliharakan Sultan" (God Bless His Majesty).

bn.label: National symbol
bn.text: Brunei's national symbol is the royal parasol.

bn.label: Independence
bn.text: Brunei became independent from the UK on 1 January 1984.

bn.label: Highest point
bn.text: The highest point in Brunei is Bukit Pagon, at 1,850 m.

bg.label: Name origin
bg.text: Named after the Bulgar tribes who settled the lower Balkan region in the 7th century A.D.; the tribal name may come from the Turkic word bulga, or "mixed," referring to the blend of Turkic and Slavic ethnicities in the tribes.

bg.label: National anthem
bg.text: The national anthem of Bulgaria is “Mila Rodino” (Dear Homeland). Composed in 1885 by a student en route to fight in the Serbo-Bulgarian War.

bg.label: National symbol
bg.text: Bulgaria's national symbol is the lion.

bg.label: World Heritage
bg.text: Bulgaria has 10 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Boyana Church and Madara Rider.

bg.label: Highest point
bg.text: The highest point in Bulgaria is Musala, at 2,925 m.

bg.label: Population
bg.text: About 6.7 million people live in Bulgaria.

bf.label: Name origin
bf.text: Name translates as "Land of the Worthy Men," from the Dyula words burkina, or "worthy," and faso, which means "land" or literally "father village," from fa, or "father," and so, or "village".

bf.label: National anthem
bf.text: The national anthem of Burkina Faso is "Le Ditanye" (Anthem of Victory). Also known as "Une Seule Nuit"(One Single Night) .

bf.label: National symbol
bf.text: Burkina Faso's national symbol is the white stallion.

bf.label: Independence
bf.text: Burkina Faso became independent from France on 5 August 1960.

bf.label: World Heritage
bf.text: Burkina Faso has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ruins of Loropéni and Ancient Ferrous Metallurgy Sites of Burkina Faso.

bf.label: Highest point
bf.text: The highest point in Burkina Faso is Tena Kourou, at 749 m.

bi.label: Name origin
bi.text: Name dates from 1966 and is derived from the name of the local Bantu people, the Rundi or Barundi; ba- is the prefix for the people, and bu- is the prefix for the country; the former name, Urundi, is the Swahili version.

bi.label: National anthem
bi.text: The national anthem of Burundi is "Burundi Bwacu" (Our Beloved Burundi).

bi.label: National symbol
bi.text: Burundi's national symbol is the lion.

bi.label: Independence
bi.text: Burundi became independent from UN trusteeship under Belgian administration on 1 July 1962.

bi.label: Highest point
bi.text: The highest point in Burundi is unnamed elevation on Mukike Range, at 2,685 m.

bi.label: Population
bi.text: About 14 million people live in Burundi.

kh.label: Name origin
kh.text: The name is derived from Kambu, a legendary ancestor of the Cambodian people.

kh.label: National anthem
kh.text: The national anthem of Cambodia is "Nokoreach" (Royal Kingdom). The anthem, based on a Cambodian folk tune, was restored after the defeat of the Communist regime.

kh.label: National symbol
kh.text: Cambodia's national symbols are the Angkor Wat temple and kouprey (wild ox).

kh.label: Independence
kh.text: Cambodia became independent from France on 9 November 1953.

kh.label: World Heritage
kh.text: Cambodia has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Angkor and Temple of Preah Vihear.

kh.label: Highest point
kh.text: The highest point in Cambodia is Phnum Aoral, at 1,810 m.

cm.label: Name origin
cm.text: In the 16th century, Portuguese explorers named an estuary near the mouth of the Wouri River the Rio dos Camaroes (River of Prawns) after the abundant shrimp in the water; the name Camaroes evolved into "Cameroon".

cm.label: National anthem
cm.text: The national anthem of Cameroon is "O Cameroun, Berceau de Nos Ancêtres" (O Cameroon, Cradle of Our Forefathers).

cm.label: National symbol
cm.text: Cameroon's national symbol is the lion.

cm.label: Independence
cm.text: Cameroon became independent from French-administered UN trusteeship on 1 January 1960.

cm.label: World Heritage
cm.text: Cameroon has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Dja Faunal Reserve and Sangha Trinational Forest.

cm.label: Highest point
cm.text: The highest point in Cameroon is Fako on Mont Cameroun, at 4,045 m.

ca.label: Name origin
ca.text: The name is probably derived from the Huron or Iroquois word kanata, meaning village or camp.

ca.label: National anthem
ca.text: The national anthem of Canada is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

ca.label: National symbol
ca.text: Canada's national symbols are the maple leaf and beaver.

ca.label: World Heritage
ca.text: Canada has 22 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including L'Anse aux Meadows and Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks.

ca.label: Highest point
ca.text: The highest point in Canada is Mount Logan, at 5,959 m.

ca.label: Population
ca.text: About 39 million people live in Canada.

cv.label: Name origin
cv.text: The name derives from the Cape Verde (Green Cape) peninsula on the Senegalese coast, the westernmost point of Africa and the nearest mainland to the islands.

cv.label: National anthem
cv.text: The national anthem of Cape Verde is "Cantico da Liberdade" (Song of Freedom).

cv.label: National symbol
cv.text: Cape Verde's national symbol is the ten five-pointed yellow stars.

cv.label: Independence
cv.text: Cape Verde became independent from Portugal on 5 July 1975.

cv.label: World Heritage
cv.text: Cape Verde has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Cidade Velha.

cv.label: Highest point
cv.text: The highest point in Cape Verde is Mt. Fogo (a volcano on Fogo Island), at 2,829 m.

cf.label: Name origin
cf.text: Self-descriptive name specifying the country's location on the continent.

cf.label: National anthem
cf.text: The national anthem of the Central African Republic is "La Renaissance" (The Renaissance). Boganda wrote the anthem's lyrics and was the first prime minister of the autonomous French territory.

cf.label: National symbol
cf.text: The Central African Republic's national symbol is the elephant.

cf.label: Independence
cf.text: The Central African Republic became independent from France on 13 August 1960.

cf.label: World Heritage
cf.text: The Central African Republic has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Manovo-Gounda St. Floris National Park and Sangha Trinational Forest.

cf.label: Highest point
cf.text: The highest point in the Central African Republic is Mont Ngaoui, at 1,410 m.

td.label: Name origin
td.text: Named for Lake Chad, which lies along the country's western border; taken from a local word meaning "large body of water" or "lake".

td.label: National anthem
td.text: The national anthem of Chad is "La Tchadienne" (The Chadian).

td.label: National symbol
td.text: Chad's national symbols are the goat (north) and lion (south).

td.label: Independence
td.text: Chad became independent from France on 11 August 1960.

td.label: World Heritage
td.text: Chad has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Lakes of Ounianga and Ennedi Massif: Natural and Cultural Landscape.

td.label: Highest point
td.text: The highest point in Chad is Emi Koussi, at 3,445 m.

cl.label: Name origin
cl.text: Derivation of the name is unclear; it may come from a local word meaning either "land's end" or "cold," or a local word that was confused with the Mexican Spanish word chili, meaning a chili pepper, in reference to the area's shape.

cl.label: National anthem
cl.text: The national anthem of Chile is "Himno Nacional de Chile" (National Anthem of Chile). Under Augusto Pinochet's military rule, a verse glorifying the army was added.

cl.label: National symbol
cl.text: Chile's national symbols are the huemul (mountain deer) and Andean condor.

cl.label: Independence
cl.text: Chile became independent from Spain on 18 September 1810.

cl.label: World Heritage
cl.text: Chile has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Rapa Nui National Park and Churches of Chiloe.

cl.label: Population
cl.text: About 19 million people live in Chile.

cn.label: Name origin
cn.text: English name could be derived from the Qin (Chin, Ts'in) rulers in the 3rd century B.C., or from the province of Shaanxi (Shensi) with its capital of Xi'an (Sian); the Chinese name Zhongguo translates as "Central Nation" or "Middle Country".

cn.label: National anthem
cn.text: The national anthem of China is "Yiyongjun Jinxingqu" (The March of the Volunteers). The anthem, which was banned during the Cultural Revolution, is more commonly known as "Zhongguo Guoge" (Chinese National Song).

cn.label: National symbol
cn.text: China's national symbols are the dragon and giant panda.

cn.label: World Heritage
cn.text: China has 60 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Imperial Palaces of the Ming and Qing Dynasties and Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor.

cn.label: Highest point
cn.text: The highest point in China is Mount Everest (highest peak in Asia and highest point on earth above sea level), at 8,849 m.

cn.label: Population
cn.text: About 1.41 billion people live in China.

co.label: National anthem
co.text: The national anthem of Colombia is "Himno Nacional de la Republica de Colombia" (National Anthem of the Republic of Colombia). The anthem comes from an inspirational poem written by President Rafael Nunez.

co.label: National symbol
co.text: Colombia's national symbol is the Andean condor.

co.label: Independence
co.text: Colombia became independent from Spain on 20 July 1810.

co.label: World Heritage
co.text: Colombia has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Chiribiquete National Park and Coffee Cultural Landscape of Colombia.

co.label: Highest point
co.text: The highest point in Colombia is Pico Cristobal Colon, at 5,730 m.

km.label: Name origin
km.text: Name derives from the Arabic al qamar, meaning "the moon".

km.label: National anthem
km.text: The national anthem of the Comoros is "Udzima wa ya Masiwa" (The Union of the Great Islands).

km.label: National symbol
km.text: The Comoros' national symbol is the four five-pointed stars and crescent moon.

km.label: Independence
km.text: The Comoros became independent from France on 6 July 1975.

km.label: Highest point
km.text: The highest point in the Comoros is Karthala, at 2,360 m.

km.label: Population
km.text: About 912,000 people live in the Comoros.

cg.label: Name origin
cg.text: Named for the Congo River, which makes up much of the country's eastern border; the river name derives from Kongo, a Bantu kingdom in the area.

cg.label: National anthem
cg.text: The national anthem of Congo is "La Congolaise" (The Congolese). Originally adopted 1959, restored 1991.

cg.label: National symbol
cg.text: Congo's national symbols are the lion and elephant.

cg.label: Independence
cg.text: Congo became independent from France on 15 August 1960.

cg.label: World Heritage
cg.text: Congo has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Sangha Trinational Forest and Forest Massif of Odzala-Kokoua.

cg.label: Highest point
cg.text: The highest point in Congo is Mont Nabeba, at 1,020 m.

cr.label: Name origin
cr.text: The name means "rich coast" in Spanish; Christopher Columbus named it in 1502, referring to the region's abundant vegetation and water.

cr.label: National anthem
cr.text: The national anthem of Costa Rica is "Himno Nacional de Costa Rica" (National Anthem of Costa Rica). The music was originally written for a welcome ceremony in 1852 for the US and UK diplomatic missions.

cr.label: National symbol
cr.text: Costa Rica's national symbol is the yiguirro (clay-colored thrush).

cr.label: Independence
cr.text: Costa Rica became independent from Spain on 15 September 1821.

cr.label: World Heritage
cr.text: Costa Rica has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Guanacaste Conservation Area and Cocos Island National Park.

cr.label: Highest point
cr.text: The highest point in Costa Rica is Cerro Chirripo, at 3,819 m.

hr.label: Name origin
hr.text: Name probably derives from the Croats, a Slavic tribe who migrated to the Balkans in the 7th century A.D., but that name may be related to the Russian word khrebet, meaning "mountain chain".

hr.label: National anthem
hr.text: The national anthem of Croatia is "Lijepa nasa domovino" (Our Beautiful Homeland). The lyrics were written in 1835, and it served as an unofficial anthem beginning in 1891.

hr.label: National symbol
hr.text: Croatia's national symbol is the red-and-white checkerboard.

hr.label: World Heritage
hr.text: Croatia has 10 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Plitvice Lakes National Park and Historic Split.

hr.label: Highest point
hr.text: The highest point in Croatia is Dinara, at 1,831 m.

hr.label: Population
hr.text: About 4.1 million people live in Croatia.

cu.label: Name origin
cu.text: The origin of the name is disputed; it could be derived from a local Taino word, either cubao, meaning "where fertile land is abundant," or coabana, meaning "great place".

cu.label: National anthem
cu.text: The national anthem of Cuba is "La Bayamesa" (The Bayamo Song). Pedro Figueredo first performed it in 1868 during the Ten Years War against the Spanish.

cu.label: National symbol
cu.text: Cuba's national symbol is the royal palm.

cu.label: World Heritage
cu.text: Cuba has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Old Havana and Trinidad and the Valley de los Ingenios.

cu.label: Highest point
cu.text: The highest point in Cuba is Pico Turquino, at 1,974 m.

cu.label: Population
cu.text: About 10 million people live in Cuba.

cy.label: Name origin
cy.text: The Greek name for the island is Kupros, which is probably derived from the Sumerian kabar, meaning "copper" or "bronze;" copper mines were located on the island in antiquity.

cy.label: National anthem
cy.text: The national anthem of Cyprus is "Ymnos eis tin Eleftherian" (Hymn to Freedom). Cyprus uses the Greek national anthem.

cy.label: National symbol
cy.text: Cyprus' national symbols are the Cypriot mouflon (wild sheep) and white dove.

cy.label: Independence
cy.text: Cyprus became independent from the UK on 16 August 1960.

cy.label: World Heritage
cy.text: Cyprus has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Paphos and Painted Churches in the Troodos Region.

cy.label: Highest point
cy.text: The highest point in Cyprus is Mount Olympus, at 1,951 m.

cz.label: Name origin
cz.text: Name derives from the Czechs, a West Slavic tribe who rose to prominence in the late 9th century A.D.; the tribal name is said to come from an ancestral chief.

cz.label: National anthem
cz.text: The national anthem of Czechia is "Kde domov muj?" (Where is My Home?). The anthem was originally written as incidental music for the play "Fidlovacka", but it soon became popular as an unofficial anthem of the Czech nation.

cz.label: National symbol
cz.text: Czechia's national symbol is the silver (or white) double-tailed rampant lion.

cz.label: World Heritage
cz.text: Czechia has 17 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Prague and Historic Telč.

cz.label: Highest point
cz.text: The highest point in Czechia is Snezka, at 1,602 m.

cz.label: Population
cz.text: About 11 million people live in Czechia.

dk.label: Name origin
dk.text: The name derives from the words Dane, a tribal name with unclear Germanic origins, and mark, a Danish word that refers to a march (borderland).

dk.label: National anthem
dk.text: The national anthem of Denmark is “Kong Christian stod ved højen mast” (King Christian Stood by the Lofty Mast). One of the oldest royal anthems in the world.

dk.label: National symbol
dk.text: Denmark's national symbols are the lion and mute swan.

dk.label: World Heritage
dk.text: Denmark has 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Denmark: Mounds, Runic Stones, and Church at Jelling and Roskilde Cathedral.

dk.label: Highest point
dk.text: The highest point in Denmark is Store Mollehoj, at 171 m.

dk.label: Population
dk.text: About 6.1 million people live in Denmark.

dj.label: Name origin
dj.text: The country name derives from the capital city of Djibouti.

dj.label: National anthem
dj.text: The national anthem of Djibouti is "Jabuuti" (Djibouti).

dj.label: National symbol
dj.text: Djibouti's national symbol is the red star.

dj.label: Independence
dj.text: Djibouti became independent from France on 27 June 1977.

dj.label: Highest point
dj.text: The highest point in Djibouti is Moussa Ali, at 2,021 m.

dj.label: Population
dj.text: About 1 million people live in Djibouti.

dm.label: Name origin
dm.text: The island was named by explorer Christopher Columbus for the day of the week on which he spotted it, Sunday (Domingo in Spanish, dominica dies in Latin), 3 November 1493.

dm.label: National anthem
dm.text: The national anthem of Dominica is "Isle of Beauty".

dm.label: National symbol
dm.text: Dominica's national symbols are the sisserou parrot and Carib wood flower.

dm.label: Independence
dm.text: Dominica became independent from the UK on 3 November 1978.

dm.label: Highest point
dm.text: The highest point in Dominica is Morne Diablotins, at 1,447 m.

do.label: Name origin
do.text: The name is a latinized form of the Spanish term Santo Domingo, meaning "holy Sunday;" Spanish explorers originally settled the island on a Sunday in 1496, and the name was first given to the island of Hispaniola as a whole in 1697.

do.label: National anthem
do.text: The national anthem of the Dominican Republic is "Himno Nacional" (National Anthem). Also known as "Quisqueyanos valientes" (Valiant Sons of Quisqueye).

do.label: National symbol
do.text: The Dominican Republic's national symbol is the palmchat (bird).

do.label: Independence
do.text: The Dominican Republic became independent from Haiti on 27 February 1844.

do.label: World Heritage
do.text: The Dominican Republic has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Colonial City of Santo Domingo.

do.label: Highest point
do.text: The highest point in the Dominican Republic is Pico Duarte, at 3,098 m.

cd.label: Name origin
cd.text: Named for the Congo River, most of which lies within the DRC; the river name derives from Kongo, a Bantu kingdom in the area.

cd.label: National anthem
cd.text: The national anthem of DR Congo is "Debout Congolaise" (Arise, Congolese). Replaced when the country was known as Zaire, but readopted in 1997.

cd.label: National symbol
cd.text: DR Congo's national symbol is the leopard.

cd.label: Independence
cd.text: DR Congo became independent from Belgium on 30 June 1960.

cd.label: World Heritage
cd.text: DR Congo has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Garamba National Park and Kahuzi-Biega National Park.

cd.label: Highest point
cd.text: The highest point in DR Congo is Pic Marguerite on Mont Ngaliema (Mount Stanley), at 5,110 m.

ec.label: Name origin
ec.text: The name is the Spanish word for "equator," referring to its geographic position.

ec.label: National anthem
ec.text: The national anthem of Ecuador is "Salve, O Patria!" (We Salute You, Our Homeland). Mera wrote the lyrics in 1865.

ec.label: National symbol
ec.text: Ecuador's national symbol is the Andean condor.

ec.label: Independence
ec.text: Ecuador became independent from Spain on 24 May 1822.

ec.label: World Heritage
ec.text: Ecuador has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Quito and Galápagos Islands.

ec.label: Population
ec.text: About 18 million people live in Ecuador.

eg.label: Name origin
eg.text: The English name Egypt derives from the ancient Greek name for the country, "Aguptos," and the ancient Roman name, "Aegyptus," with the Greek form coming from the words aia gupos, or "land of the vulture;" the Arabic name for the country,…

eg.label: National anthem
eg.text: The national anthem of Egypt is "Bilady, Bilady, Bilady" (My Homeland, My Homeland, My Homeland). The current anthem was written after the 1979 peace treaty with Israel.

eg.label: National symbol
eg.text: Egypt's national symbols are the golden eagle and white lotus.

eg.label: Independence
eg.text: Egypt became independent from UK protectorate status; the military-led revolution that began on 23 July 1952 led to a republic being declared on 18 June 1953 and all British troops withdrawn on 18 June 1956 on 28 February 1922.

eg.label: World Heritage
eg.text: Egypt has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Memphis and its Necropolis and Ancient Thebes with its Necropolis.

eg.label: Highest point
eg.text: The highest point in Egypt is Mount Catherine, at 2,629 m.

sv.label: Name origin
sv.text: Means "the Savior" in Spanish and is a shortened form of "the Divine Savior of the World" (el Divino Salvador del Mundo), referring to Jesus Christ.

sv.label: National anthem
sv.text: The national anthem of El Salvador is "Himno Nacional de El Salvador" (National Anthem of El Salvador). Officially adopted 1953, in use since 1879.

sv.label: National symbol
sv.text: El Salvador's national symbol is the turquoise-browed motmot (bird).

sv.label: Independence
sv.text: El Salvador became independent from Spain on 15 September 1821.

sv.label: World Heritage
sv.text: El Salvador has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Joya de Cerén Archaeological Site.

sv.label: Highest point
sv.text: The highest point in El Salvador is Cerro El Pital, at 2,730 m.

gq.label: Name origin
gq.text: The country is named for the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea and stretches north to the Sahel; the "equatorial" refers to the fact that the country lies just north of the Equator.

gq.label: National anthem
gq.text: The national anthem of Equatorial Guinea is "Caminemos pisando la senda" (Let Us Tread the Path).

gq.label: National symbol
gq.text: Equatorial Guinea's national symbol is the silk cotton tree.

gq.label: Independence
gq.text: Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain on 12 October 1968.

gq.label: Highest point
gq.text: The highest point in Equatorial Guinea is Pico Basile, at 3,008 m.

gq.label: Population
gq.text: About 1.8 million people live in Equatorial Guinea.

er.label: Name origin
er.text: The country name derives from the ancient Greek name Erythra Thalassa, meaning "Red Sea," the body of water that borders the country.

er.label: National anthem
er.text: The national anthem of Eritrea is "Ertra, Ertra, Ertra" (Eritrea, Eritrea, Eritrea).

er.label: National symbol
er.text: Eritrea's national symbol is the camel.

er.label: Independence
er.text: Eritrea became independent from Ethiopia on 24 May 1993.

er.label: World Heritage
er.text: Eritrea has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Asmara: A Modernist African City.

er.label: Highest point
er.text: The highest point in Eritrea is Soira, at 3,018 m.

ee.label: Name origin
ee.text: Derives from the name of the people who lived along the eastern Baltic Sea in the first centuries A.D., which came from the Baltic word aueist, meaning "waterside dwellers".

ee.label: National anthem
ee.text: The national anthem of Estonia is "Mu isamaa, mu onn ja room" (My Native Land, My Pride and Joy). Unofficially in use since 1869, it has the same melody as Finland's anthem, but with different lyrics.

ee.label: National symbol
ee.text: Estonia's national symbols are the barn swallow and cornflower.

ee.label: World Heritage
ee.text: Estonia has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Center (Old Town) of Tallinn and Struve Geodetic Arc.

ee.label: Highest point
ee.text: The highest point in Estonia is Suur Munamagi, at 318 m.

ee.label: Population
ee.text: About 1.3 million people live in Estonia.

sz.label: Name origin
sz.text: The country name derives from 19th century King Mswati II, under whose rule Swati territory was expanded and unified.

sz.label: National anthem
sz.text: The national anthem of Eswatini is "Nkulunkulu Mnikati wetibusiso temaSwati" (O God, Bestower of the Blessings of the Swazi). Uses elements of both ethnic Swazi and Western music styles.

sz.label: National symbol
sz.text: Eswatini's national symbols are the lion and elephant.

sz.label: Independence
sz.text: Eswatini became independent from the UK on 6 September 1968.

sz.label: Highest point
sz.text: The highest point in Eswatini is Emlembe, at 1,862 m.

sz.label: Population
sz.text: About 1.1 million people live in Eswatini.

et.label: Name origin
et.text: The country name derives from the ancient Greek word used to describe the inhabitants, aithiops, meaning "burnt appearance".

et.label: National anthem
et.text: The national anthem of Ethiopia is "Whedefit Gesgeshi Woud Enat Ethiopia" (March Forward, Dear Mother Ethiopia).

et.label: National symbol
et.text: Ethiopia's national symbols are the Abyssinian lion (traditional) and yellow pentagram with five rays of light on a blue field (promoted by government).

et.label: World Heritage
et.text: Ethiopia has 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela and Simien National Park.

et.label: Highest point
et.text: The highest point in Ethiopia is Ras Dejen, at 4,550 m.

et.label: Population
et.text: About 121 million people live in Ethiopia.

fj.label: Name origin
fj.text: The Fijians called their home Viti, but the neighboring Tongans called it Fisi; in the Anglicized spelling of the Tongan pronunciation -- promulgated by explorer Captain James Cook -- the designation became Fiji.

fj.label: National anthem
fj.text: The national anthem of Fiji is "God Bless Fiji" (Let Us Show Pride). Known in Fijian as "Meda Dau Doka" (Let Us Show Pride).

fj.label: National symbol
fj.text: Fiji's national symbol is the Fijian canoe.

fj.label: Independence
fj.text: Fiji became independent from the UK on 10 October 1970.

fj.label: World Heritage
fj.text: Fiji has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Levuka Historical Port Town.

fj.label: Highest point
fj.text: The highest point in Fiji is Tomanivi, at 1,324 m.

fi.label: Name origin
fi.text: Name derives from the Finns, an ethnic group in northeastern Europe; their name comes from the Germanic word finna, meaning "fish scale;" the local name, Suomi, may come from two local words: suo, meaning "marsh," and maa, meaning "land".

fi.label: National anthem
fi.text: The national anthem of Finland is "Maamme" (Our Land). In use since 1848.

fi.label: National symbol
fi.text: Finland's national symbol is the lion.

fi.label: Independence
fi.text: Finland became independent from Russia on 6 December 1917.

fi.label: World Heritage
fi.text: Finland has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Fortress of Suomenlinna and Old Rauma.

fi.label: Highest point
fi.text: The highest point in Finland is Halti (alternatively Haltia, Haltitunturi, Haltiatunturi), at 1,328 m.

fr.label: Name origin
fr.text: Derives from the Latin name Francia, meaning "Land of the Franks"; the Franks were a group of Germanic tribes located along the middle and lower Rhine River in the 3rd century A.D.

fr.label: National anthem
fr.text: The national anthem of France is "La Marseillaise" (The Song of Marseille). Acquired its name when the National Guard of Marseille sang the song while marching into Paris in 1792 during the French Revolution.

fr.label: National symbol
fr.text: France's national symbols are the Gallic rooster, fleur-de-lis and Marianne (female personification of the country).

fr.label: World Heritage
fr.text: France has 54 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Chartres Cathedral and Palace and Park of Versailles.

fr.label: Population
fr.text: About 69 million people live in France.

fr.label: Capital
fr.text: The capital of France is Paris.

ga.label: Name origin
ga.text: Name originates from the Portuguese word gabão, meaning "cloak," possibly used by early explorers to describe the shape of the Komo River estuary.

ga.label: National anthem
ga.text: The national anthem of Gabon is "La Concorde" (The Concorde).

ga.label: National symbol
ga.text: Gabon's national symbol is the black panther.

ga.label: Independence
ga.text: Gabon became independent from France on 17 August 1960.

ga.label: World Heritage
ga.text: Gabon has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ecosystem and Relict Cultural Landscape of Lopé-Okanda and Ivindo National Park.

ga.label: Highest point
ga.text: The highest point in Gabon is Mont Bengoue, at 1,050 m.

gm.label: Name origin
gm.text: Named for the Gambia River that flows through the country; Portuguese explorers in the 15th century derived the name for the river from its local name, Ba-Dimma, meaning "the river".

gm.label: National anthem
gm.text: The national anthem of the Gambia is "For The Gambia, Our Homeland". The music is an adaptation of the traditional Mandinka song "Foday Kaba Dumbuya".

gm.label: National symbol
gm.text: The Gambia's national symbol is the lion.

gm.label: Independence
gm.text: The Gambia became independent from the UK on 18 February 1965.

gm.label: World Heritage
gm.text: The Gambia has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites and Stone Circles of Senegambia.

gm.label: Population
gm.text: About 2.5 million people live in the Gambia.

ge.label: Name origin
ge.text: The Western name probably derives from the name of the local people, the Gurz, whose name origin is uncertain; the native name "Sak'art'velo" means "Land of the Kartvelians" and refers to the core central Georgian region of Kartli.

ge.label: National anthem
ge.text: The national anthem of Georgia is "Tavisupleba" (Liberty). Based on music from the operas "Abesalom da Eteri" and "Daisi".

ge.label: National symbol
ge.text: Georgia's national symbols are the Saint George and lion.

ge.label: World Heritage
ge.text: Georgia has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Gelati Monastery and Historical Monuments of Mtskheta.

ge.label: Highest point
ge.text: The highest point in Georgia is Mt'a Shkhara, at 5,193 m.

ge.label: Population
ge.text: About 4.9 million people live in Georgia.

de.label: Name origin
de.text: The origin of the name is unclear; it may come from Celtic words meaning "neighboring people," or it may derive from Germanic words meaning either "spear man" or "head man;" the native designation "Deutsch" comes from the Old High German…

de.label: National anthem
de.text: The national anthem of Germany is “Lied der Deutschen”(Song of the Germans). First adopted 1922.

de.label: National symbol
de.text: Germany's national symbol is the eagle.

de.label: World Heritage
de.text: Germany has 56 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Museumsinsel (Museum Island), Berlin and Palaces and Parks of Potsdam and Berlin.

de.label: Highest point
de.text: The highest point in Germany is Zugspitze, at 2,963 m.

de.label: Population
de.text: About 84 million people live in Germany.

gh.label: Name origin
gh.text: Named for a tribal chieftain who ruled a large part of the region prior to the 13th century, even though his territory was northwest of modern-day Ghana.

gh.label: National anthem
gh.text: The national anthem of Ghana is "God Bless Our Homeland Ghana". The lyrics were changed twice, in 1960 when a republic was declared and after a 1966 coup.

gh.label: National symbol
gh.text: Ghana's national symbols are the black star and golden eagle.

gh.label: Independence
gh.text: Ghana became independent from the UK on 6 March 1957.

gh.label: World Heritage
gh.text: Ghana has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Forts and Castles, Volta, Greater Accra, Central and Western Regions and Asante Traditional Buildings.

gh.label: Highest point
gh.text: The highest point in Ghana is Mount Afadjato, at 885 m.

gr.label: Name origin
gr.text: The English name derives from the Roman (Latin) designation Graecia, meaning "Land of the Greeks"; the Greeks call their country Ellas or Ellada, which is probably derived from Hellas, the name of the mythical son of Deucalian.

gr.label: National anthem
gr.text: The national anthem of Greece is "Ymnos eis tin Eleftherian" (Hymn to Freedom).

gr.label: National symbol
gr.text: Greece's national symbol is the Greek cross (white cross on a blue field).

gr.label: Independence
gr.text: Greece became independent from the Ottoman Empire on 3 February 1830.

gr.label: World Heritage
gr.text: Greece has 20 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Acropolis, Athens and Archaeological site of Delphi.

gr.label: Population
gr.text: About 10 million people live in Greece.

gd.label: Name origin
gd.text: Origin of the name remains obscure; some sources attribute the designation to Spanish influence (most likely named for the Spanish city of Granada); in Spanish granada means "pomegranate".

gd.label: National anthem
gd.text: The national anthem of Grenada is "God Save the King". Royal anthem, as a Commonwealth country.

gd.label: National symbol
gd.text: Grenada's national symbols are the Grenada dove and bougainvillea flower.

gd.label: Independence
gd.text: Grenada became independent from the UK on 7 February 1974.

gd.label: Highest point
gd.text: The highest point in Grenada is Mount Saint Catherine, at 840 m.

gt.label: Name origin
gt.text: The Spanish conquistadors' first capital (established in 1524) was a former Mayan settlement called "Quauhtemallan" by their Nahuatl-speaking Mexican allies, a name that means "land of the eagle" but that the Spanish probably pronounced…

gt.label: National anthem
gt.text: The national anthem of Guatemala is "Himno Nacional de Guatemala" (National Anthem of Guatemala).

gt.label: National symbol
gt.text: Guatemala's national symbol is the quetzal (bird).

gt.label: Independence
gt.text: Guatemala became independent from Spain on 15 September 1821.

gt.label: World Heritage
gt.text: Guatemala has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Antigua Guatemala and Tikal National Park.

gt.label: Highest point
gt.text: The highest point in Guatemala is Volcan Tajumulco (highest point in Central America), at 4,220 m.

gn.label: Name origin
gn.text: The country is named after the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea, but the name itself derives from the Tuareg word aginaw, meaning "black people".

gn.label: National anthem
gn.text: The national anthem of Guinea is "Liberté" (Liberty).

gn.label: National symbol
gn.text: Guinea's national symbol is the elephant.

gn.label: Independence
gn.text: Guinea became independent from France on 2 October 1958.

gn.label: World Heritage
gn.text: Guinea has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve.

gn.label: Highest point
gn.text: The highest point in Guinea is Mont Nimba, at 1,752 m.

gw.label: Name origin
gw.text: The country is partly named after the Guinea region of West Africa that lies along the Gulf of Guinea.

gw.label: National anthem
gw.text: The national anthem of Guinea-Bissau is "Esta e a Nossa Patria Bem Amada" (This is Our Beloved Country). A delegation from Portuguese Guinea visited China in 1963 and heard music by Xiao He.

gw.label: National symbol
gw.text: Guinea-Bissau's national symbol is the black star.

gw.label: World Heritage
gw.text: Guinea-Bissau has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Coastal and Marine Ecosystems of the Bijagós Archipelago – Omatí Minhô.

gw.label: Highest point
gw.text: The highest point in Guinea-Bissau is Dongol Ronde, at 277 m.

gw.label: Population
gw.text: About 2.1 million people live in Guinea-Bissau.

gy.label: Name origin
gy.text: The name is derived from Guiana, the original name for the region that included British Guiana, Dutch Guiana, and French Guiana.

gy.label: National anthem
gy.text: The national anthem of Guyana is "Dear Land of Guyana, of Rivers and Plains".

gy.label: National symbol
gy.text: Guyana's national symbols are the Canje pheasant (hoatzin), jaguar and Victoria Regia water lily.

gy.label: Independence
gy.text: Guyana became independent from the UK on 26 May 1966.

gy.label: Highest point
gy.text: The highest point in Guyana is Laberintos del Norte on Mount Roraima, at 2,775 m.

ht.label: Name origin
ht.text: Derived from the Arawak name Ayti, meaning "Land of Mountains," that was originally applied to the entire island of Hispaniola.

ht.label: National anthem
ht.text: The national anthem of Haiti is "La Dessalinienne" (The Dessalines Song). Named for Jean-Jacques Dessalines, founder of Haiti.

ht.label: National symbol
ht.text: Haiti's national symbols are the Hispaniolan trogon (bird) and hibiscus flower.

ht.label: Independence
ht.text: Haiti became independent from France on 1 January 1804.

ht.label: World Heritage
ht.text: Haiti has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: National History Park – Citadel, Sans Souci, Ramiers.

ht.label: Highest point
ht.text: The highest point in Haiti is Pic la Selle, at 2,674 m.

hn.label: Name origin
hn.text: The name means "depths" in Spanish and refers to the deep anchorage in the northern Bay of Trujillo.

hn.label: National anthem
hn.text: The national anthem of Honduras is "Himno Nacional de Honduras" (National Anthem of Honduras). The anthem's seven verses chronicle Honduran history.

hn.label: National symbol
hn.text: Honduras' national symbols are the scarlet macaw and white-tailed deer.

hn.label: Independence
hn.text: Honduras became independent from Spain on 15 September 1821.

hn.label: World Heritage
hn.text: Honduras has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Maya Site of Copan and Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve.

hn.label: Highest point
hn.text: The highest point in Honduras is Cerro Las Minas, at 2,870 m.

hu.label: Name origin
hu.text: The Byzantine Greeks referred to the tribes that arrived on the steppes of Eastern Europe in the 9th century as the "Oungroi," a name that later became "Hungari," which originally meant an "[alliance of] ten tribes;" the Hungarian name…

hu.label: National anthem
hu.text: The national anthem of Hungary is "Himnusz" (Hymn).

hu.label: National symbol
hu.text: Hungary's national symbol is the Holy Crown of Hungary (Crown of Saint Stephen).

hu.label: World Heritage
hu.text: Hungary has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Budapest, including the Banks of the Danube, the Buda Castle Quarter, and Andrássy Avenue and Old Village of Hollókő and its Surroundings.

hu.label: Highest point
hu.text: The highest point in Hungary is Kekes, at 1,014 m.

hu.label: Population
hu.text: About 9.9 million people live in Hungary.

is.label: Name origin
is.text: Floki Vilgerdarson, an early Norse explorer of the island in the 10th century, applied the name "Land of Ice," from the local words ís (ice) and land (land).

is.label: National anthem
is.text: The national anthem of Iceland is "Lofsongur" (Song of Praise).

is.label: National symbol
is.text: Iceland's national symbol is the gyrfalcon.

is.label: World Heritage
is.text: Iceland has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Thingvellir National Park and Surtsey.

is.label: Highest point
is.text: The highest point in Iceland is Hvannadalshnukur (at Vatnajokull Glacier), at 2,110 m.

in.label: Name origin
in.text: The English name derives from the Indus River; the Indian name, Bharat, may derive from the Bharatas tribe mentioned in the Sanskrit Vedas (Hindu religious texts).

in.label: National anthem
in.text: The national anthem of India is "Jana-Gana-Mana" (Thou Art the Ruler of the Minds of All People). Rabindranath Tagore, a Nobel laureate, also wrote Bangladesh's national anthem.

in.label: Independence
in.text: India became independent from the UK on 15 August 1947.

in.label: World Heritage
in.text: India has 44 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Taj Mahal and Agra Fort.

in.label: Highest point
in.text: The highest point in India is Kanchenjunga, at 8,586 m.

in.label: Population
in.text: About 1.42 billion people live in India.

id.label: Name origin
id.text: The name is an 18th-century construct of two Greek words, "Indos" (India) and "nesoi" (islands), meaning "Indian islands".

id.label: National anthem
id.text: The national anthem of Indonesia is "Indonesia Raya" (Great Indonesia).

id.label: National symbol
id.text: Indonesia's national symbol is the garuda (mythical bird).

id.label: World Heritage
id.text: Indonesia has 10 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Borobudur Temple Compounds and Komodo National Park.

id.label: Highest point
id.text: The highest point in Indonesia is Puncak Jaya, at 4,884 m.

id.label: Population
id.text: About 284 million people live in Indonesia.

ir.label: Name origin
ir.text: The name derives from the Sanskrit word arya, referring to people living in a mountainous land, from the root word ar-, or "mountain;" the former name, Persia, was originally "Pars" (or the Arabic-influenced variant "Fars") from the Old…

ir.label: National anthem
ir.text: The national anthem of Iran is "Soroud-e Melli-ye Jomhouri-ye Eslami-ye Iran" (National Anthem of the Islamic Republic of Iran).

ir.label: National symbol
ir.text: Iran's national symbol is the lion.

ir.label: World Heritage
ir.text: Iran has 29 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Persepolis and Tchogha Zanbil.

ir.label: Highest point
ir.text: The highest point in Iran is Kuh-e Damavand, at 5,625 m.

ir.label: Population
ir.text: About 89 million people live in Iran.

iq.label: Name origin
iq.text: The name probably derives from Uruk ("Erech" in Aramaic), the ancient Sumerian and Babylonian city on the Euphrates River.

iq.label: National anthem
iq.text: The national anthem of Iraq is "Mawtini" (My Homeland). Popular Arab folk song that also serves as an unofficial anthem for the Palestinian people.

iq.label: National symbol
iq.text: Iraq's national symbol is the golden eagle.

iq.label: Independence
iq.text: Iraq became independent from League of Nations mandate under British administration on 3 October 1932.

iq.label: World Heritage
iq.text: Iraq has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ashur (Qal'at Sherqat) and Babylon.

iq.label: Highest point
iq.text: The highest point in Iraq is Cheekha Dar (Kurdish for "Black Tent"), at 3,611 m.

ie.label: Name origin
ie.text: The Irish name Eire evolved from the Gaelic name Eriu, which is possibly derived from the Old Celtic iveriu, meaning "good land;" the English name, Ireland, is a direct translation.

ie.label: National anthem
ie.text: The national anthem of Ireland is "Amhran na bhFiann" (The Soldier's Song). The song "Ireland's Call" is often used as the anthem at athletic events if citizens of Ireland and Northern Ireland are competing as a unified team.

ie.label: National symbol
ie.text: Ireland's national symbols are the harp and shamrock (trefoil).

ie.label: World Heritage
ie.text: Ireland has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Brú na Bóinne - Archaeological Ensemble of the Bend of the Boyne and Sceilg Mhichíl.

ie.label: Highest point
ie.text: The highest point in Ireland is Carrauntoohil, at 1,041 m.

ie.label: Population
ie.text: About 5.2 million people live in Ireland.

il.label: Name origin
il.text: Named after the ancient Kingdom of Israel; according to Biblical tradition, the Jewish patriarch Jacob received the name Israel (meaning "He who struggles with God") after he wrestled with an angel of the Lord.

il.label: National anthem
il.text: The national anthem of Israel is "Hatikvah" (The Hope). Used as the anthem of the Zionist movement since 1897.

il.label: National symbol
il.text: Israel's national symbols are the Star of David (Magen David) and menorah (seven-branched lampstand).

il.label: World Heritage
il.text: Israel has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Masada and Old City of Acre.

il.label: Population
il.text: About 9.4 million people live in Israel.

il.label: Capital
il.text: The capital of Israel is Jerusalem.

it.label: Name origin
it.text: Derivation is unclear; traditionally said to come from the Vitali, a tribe that settled in what is now Calabria, and whose name is believed to be linked to the Latin word vitulus, or "calf;" alternatively, the name may derive from a local…

it.label: National anthem
it.text: The national anthem of Italy is "Il Canto degli Italiani" (The Song of the Italians). The anthem, originally written in 1847, is also known as "L'Inno di Mameli" (Mameli's Hymn), and "Fratelli d'Italia" (Brothers of Italy).

it.label: National symbol
it.text: Italy's national symbol is the five-pointed white star (Stella d'Italia).

it.label: World Heritage
it.text: Italy has 61 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Center of Rome and Archaeological Areas of Pompeii, Herculaneum, and Torre Annunziata.

it.label: Highest point
it.text: The highest point in Italy is Mont Blanc (Monte Bianco) de Courmayeur (a secondary peak of Mont Blanc), at 4,748 m.

it.label: Population
it.text: About 61 million people live in Italy.

ci.label: Name origin
ci.text: Name, which means "Ivory Coast" in French, reflects the ivory trade in the region from the 15th to 17th centuries; the French version of the name has been used internationally since 1986, at the country's request.

ci.label: National anthem
ci.text: The national anthem of Ivory Coast is "L'Abidjanaise" (Song of Abidjan). Named after the former capital city of Abidjan.

ci.label: National symbol
ci.text: Ivory Coast's national symbol is the elephant.

ci.label: Independence
ci.text: Ivory Coast became independent from France on 7 August 1960.

ci.label: World Heritage
ci.text: Ivory Coast has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Comoé National Park and Historic Grand-Bassam.

ci.label: Highest point
ci.text: The highest point in Ivory Coast is Monts Nimba, at 1,752 m.

jm.label: Name origin
jm.text: From the Arawak word xaymaca, meaning "Land of Wood and Water" or possibly "Land of Springs".

jm.label: National anthem
jm.text: The national anthem of Jamaica is "Jamaica, Land We Love".

jm.label: National symbol
jm.text: Jamaica's national symbols are the green-and-black streamertail (bird) and guaiacwood (Guiacum officinale).

jm.label: Independence
jm.text: Jamaica became independent from the UK on 6 August 1962.

jm.label: World Heritage
jm.text: Jamaica has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Blue and John Crow Mountains and The Archaeological Ensemble of 17th Century Port Royal.

jm.label: Highest point
jm.text: The highest point in Jamaica is Blue Mountain Peak, at 2,256 m.

jp.label: Name origin
jp.text: The English word for Japan comes from the Chinese name for the country, Cipangu; both Nihon and Nippon come from the Japanese words nichi, or "sun," and hon, or "origin," which is frequently translated as "Land of the Rising Sun".

jp.label: National anthem
jp.text: The national anthem of Japan is "Kimigayo" (His Majesty’s Reign). Unofficial national anthem since 1883.

jp.label: National symbol
jp.text: Japan's national symbols are the red sun disc and chrysanthemum.

jp.label: World Heritage
jp.text: Japan has 26 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Buddhist Monuments in the Horyu-ji Area and Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara.

jp.label: Highest point
jp.text: The highest point in Japan is Mount Fuji, at 3,776 m.

jp.label: Population
jp.text: About 123 million people live in Japan.

jo.label: Name origin
jo.text: Named for the Jordan River, which makes up part of Jordan's northwest border; the origin of the river's name is unclear, but it may come from a local word meaning "river".

jo.label: National anthem
jo.text: The national anthem of Jordan is "As-salam al-malaki al-urdoni" (Long Live the King of Jordan). The shortened version of the anthem is most commonly used.

jo.label: National symbol
jo.text: Jordan's national symbol is the eagle.

jo.label: Independence
jo.text: Jordan became independent from League of Nations mandate under British administration on 25 May 1946.

jo.label: World Heritage
jo.text: Jordan has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Petra and Quseir Amra.

jo.label: Highest point
jo.text: The highest point in Jordan is Jabal Umm ad Dami, at 1,854 m.

kz.label: Name origin
kz.text: The name may derive from the Turkic word kazak, meaning "nomad;" the Persian suffix -stan means "place of" or "country".

kz.label: National anthem
kz.text: The national anthem of Kazakhstan is "Menin Qazaqstanim" (My Kazakhstan). President Nursultan Nazarbayev played a role in revising the lyrics.

kz.label: National symbol
kz.text: Kazakhstan's national symbol is the golden eagle.

kz.label: Independence
kz.text: Kazakhstan became independent from the Soviet Union on 16 December 1991.

kz.label: World Heritage
kz.text: Kazakhstan has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi and Petroglyphs at Tanbaly.

kz.label: Population
kz.text: About 20 million people live in Kazakhstan.

ke.label: Name origin
ke.text: Named for Mount Kenya; the mountain's name may derive from the Kikuyu word kere nyaga, or "white mountain".

ke.label: National anthem
ke.text: The national anthem of Kenya is "Ee Mungu Nguvu Yetu" (O God of All Creation). Based on a traditional Kenyan folk song.

ke.label: National symbol
ke.text: Kenya's national symbol is the lion.

ke.label: Independence
ke.text: Kenya became independent from the UK on 12 December 1963.

ke.label: World Heritage
ke.text: Kenya has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Lake Turkana National Parks and Mount Kenya National Park/Natural Forest.

ke.label: Highest point
ke.text: The highest point in Kenya is Mount Kenya, at 5,199 m.

ki.label: Name origin
ki.text: The name is the local pronunciation of "Gilbert," the former designation of the islands; originally named after explorer Thomas Gilbert, who mapped many of the islands in 1788.

ki.label: National anthem
ki.text: The national anthem of Kiribati is "Teirake kaini Kiribati" (Stand Up, Kiribati).

ki.label: National symbol
ki.text: Kiribati's national symbol is the frigatebird.

ki.label: Independence
ki.text: Kiribati became independent from the UK on 12 July 1979.

ki.label: World Heritage
ki.text: Kiribati has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Phoenix Islands Protected Area.

ki.label: Highest point
ki.text: The highest point in Kiribati is unnamed elevation on Banaba, at 81 m.

kw.label: Name origin
kw.text: The name derives from the capital city, which comes from the Arabic al-kuwayt, itself a diminutive of the Hindustani term kut, meaning a fortress-like house.

kw.label: National anthem
kw.text: The national anthem of Kuwait is "Al-Nasheed Al-Watani" (National Anthem). The anthem is only used on formal occasions.

kw.label: National symbol
kw.text: Kuwait's national symbol is the golden falcon.

kw.label: Independence
kw.text: Kuwait became independent from the UK on 19 June 1961.

kw.label: Highest point
kw.text: The highest point in Kuwait is 3.6 km W. of Al-Salmi Border Post, at 300 m.

kw.label: Population
kw.text: About 3.2 million people live in Kuwait.

kg.label: Name origin
kg.text: Named for the local Kyrgyz people, with "-stan" coming from the Persian word ostan, meaning "country;" the Kyrgyz name may derive from the Turkic root words kir, or "steppe," and gismek, "to wander;" the name is traditionally said to come…

kg.label: National anthem
kg.text: The national anthem of Kyrgyzstan is "Kyrgyz Respublikasynyn Mamlekettik Gimni" (National Anthem of the Kyrgyz Republic).

kg.label: National symbol
kg.text: Kyrgyzstan's national symbol is the white falcon.

kg.label: Independence
kg.text: Kyrgyzstan became independent from the Soviet Union on 31 August 1991.

kg.label: World Heritage
kg.text: Kyrgyzstan has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Sulaiman-Too Sacred Mountain and Silk Roads: the Chang'an-Tianshan Corridor.

kg.label: Highest point
kg.text: The highest point in Kyrgyzstan is Jengish Chokusu (Pik Pobedy), at 7,439 m.

la.label: Name origin
la.text: Name means "Land of the Lao [people];" it derives from the name of the country's founder, Lao.

la.label: National anthem
la.text: The national anthem of Laos is "Pheng Xat Lao" (Hymn of the Lao People). The anthem's lyrics were changed after the communist revolution that overthrew the monarchy in 1975.

la.label: National symbol
la.text: Laos' national symbol is the elephant.

la.label: World Heritage
la.text: Laos has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Town of Luangphrabang and Vat Phou and Associated Ancient Settlements.

la.label: Highest point
la.text: The highest point in Laos is Phu Bia, at 2,817 m.

la.label: Population
la.text: About 8 million people live in Laos.

lv.label: Name origin
lv.text: The name originates from the Latgalians, one of four eastern Baltic tribes that formed the ethnic core of the Latvian people (ca. 8th-12th centuries A.D.).

lv.label: National anthem
lv.text: The national anthem of Latvia is "Dievs, sveti Latviju!" (God Bless Latvia). First performed in 1873 when Latvia was part of Russia.

lv.label: National symbol
lv.text: Latvia's national symbol is the white wagtail (bird).

lv.label: World Heritage
lv.text: Latvia has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Center of Riga and Struve Geodetic Arc.

lv.label: Highest point
lv.text: The highest point in Latvia is Gaizina Kalns, at 312 m.

lv.label: Population
lv.text: About 1.9 million people live in Latvia.

lb.label: Name origin
lb.text: Derives from the Semitic root lbn, meaning "white," and probably refers to the country's snow-capped mountains.

lb.label: National anthem
lb.text: The national anthem of Lebanon is "Kulluna lil-watan" (All of Us, For Our Country!).

lb.label: National symbol
lb.text: Lebanon's national symbol is the cedar tree.

lb.label: Independence
lb.text: Lebanon became independent from League of Nations mandate under French administration on 22 November 1943.

lb.label: World Heritage
lb.text: Lebanon has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Anjar and Baalbek.

lb.label: Highest point
lb.text: The highest point in Lebanon is Qornet es Saouda, at 3,088 m.

ls.label: Name origin
ls.text: The name comes from the Sotho people, whose name means "dark-skinned;" Le- is a singular noun prefix; the former name, Basutoland, uses the plural noun prefix, Ba-.

ls.label: National anthem
ls.text: The national anthem of Lesotho is "Lesotho fatse la bo ntat'a rona" (Lesotho, Land of Our Fathers).

ls.label: National symbol
ls.text: Lesotho's national symbol is the mokorotio (Basotho hat).

ls.label: Independence
ls.text: Lesotho became independent from the UK on 4 October 1966.

ls.label: World Heritage
ls.text: Lesotho has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Maloti-Drakensberg Park.

ls.label: Highest point
ls.text: The highest point in Lesotho is Thabana Ntlenyana, at 3,482 m.

lr.label: Name origin
lr.text: Name derives from the Latin word liber, meaning "free;" so named because the nation was created as a homeland for liberated African-American slaves.

lr.label: National anthem
lr.text: The national anthem of Liberia is "All Hail, Liberia, Hail!". The anthem's author later became the third president of Liberia.

lr.label: National symbol
lr.text: Liberia's national symbol is the white star.

lr.label: Highest point
lr.text: The highest point in Liberia is Mount Wuteve, at 1,447 m.

lr.label: Population
lr.text: About 5.6 million people live in Liberia.

lr.label: Capital
lr.text: The capital of Liberia is Monrovia.

ly.label: Name origin
ly.text: The name probably derives from the Libu, a North African tribe first mentioned in texts from the 13th century B.C.; the ancient Greeks and Romans used the name for the entire North African coast west of Egypt.

ly.label: National anthem
ly.text: The national anthem of Libya is "Libya, Libya, Libya". Readopted 2011 with some modification to the lyrics.

ly.label: National symbol
ly.text: Libya's national symbols are the star and crescent and hawk.

ly.label: Independence
ly.text: Libya became independent from UN trusteeship on 24 December 1951.

ly.label: World Heritage
ly.text: Libya has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Archaeological Site of Cyrene and Archaeological Site of Leptis Magna, Archaeological Site of Sabratha.

ly.label: Highest point
ly.text: The highest point in Libya is Bikku Bitti, at 2,267 m.

li.label: Name origin
li.text: Named after the Liechtenstein family that purchased and united the counties of Schellenburg and Vaduz in 1719; the family name was taken from its Austrian castle of the same name, which in German means "light stone".

li.label: National anthem
li.text: The national anthem of Liechtenstein is "Oben am jungen Rhein" (High Above the Young Rhine). Uses the tune of the United Kingdom's anthem, "God Save the King".

li.label: National symbol
li.text: Liechtenstein's national symbol is the princely hat (crown).

li.label: Highest point
li.text: The highest point in Liechtenstein is Vorder-Grauspitz, at 2,599 m.

li.label: Capital
li.text: The capital of Liechtenstein is Vaduz.

lt.label: Name origin
lt.text: Meaning of the name is obscure; may be derived from the local words lietava, meaning "small river," or lietus, meaning "rain" or "land of rain," or the Latin word litus, meaning "shore".

lt.label: National anthem
lt.text: The national anthem of Lithuania is "Tautiska giesme" (The National Song). Written in 1898 when Lithuania was part of Russia.

lt.label: National symbol
lt.text: Lithuania's national symbols are the mounted knight known as Vytis (the Chaser) and white stork.

lt.label: World Heritage
lt.text: Lithuania has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Vilnius Historic Center and Curonian Spit.

lt.label: Highest point
lt.text: The highest point in Lithuania is Aukstojas, at 294 m.

lt.label: Population
lt.text: About 2.8 million people live in Lithuania.

lu.label: Name origin
lu.text: Probably derived from an early Celtic or Germanic form of the name, Lucilinburhuc, that was thought to mean "little fortress;" the name first referred to the city and was later used for the country.

lu.label: National anthem
lu.text: The national anthem of Luxembourg is “De Wilhelmus” (The William). Royal anthem, for use when members of the grand ducal family enter or exit a ceremony in Luxembourg.

lu.label: National symbol
lu.text: Luxembourg's national symbol is the red rampant lion.

lu.label: World Heritage
lu.text: Luxembourg has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Luxembourg City Old Quarters and Fortifications.

lu.label: Highest point
lu.text: The highest point in Luxembourg is Buurgplaatz, at 559 m.

mg.label: Name origin
mg.text: A variant of the name was first used by 13th-century Venetian explorer Marco Polo when he confused the island with the Somali port of Mogadishu; the transliteration was later adopted as the official name.

mg.label: National anthem
mg.text: The national anthem of Madagascar is "Ry Tanindraza nay malala o" (O Our Beloved Fatherland).

mg.label: National symbol
mg.text: Madagascar's national symbols are the traveller's palm (ravenala) and zebu.

mg.label: Independence
mg.text: Madagascar became independent from France on 26 June 1960.

mg.label: World Heritage
mg.text: Madagascar has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Tsingy de Bemaraha Strict Nature Reserve and Ambohimanga Royal Hill.

mg.label: Highest point
mg.text: The highest point in Madagascar is Maromokotro, at 2,876 m.

mw.label: Name origin
mw.text: Named for the Maravi people who inhabited the area since the 14th century; the word maravi means "flames".

mw.label: National anthem
mw.text: The national anthem of Malawi is "Mulungu dalitsa Malawi" (O God, Bless Our Land of Malawi).

mw.label: National symbol
mw.text: Malawi's national symbol is the lion.

mw.label: Independence
mw.text: Malawi became independent from the UK on 6 July 1964.

mw.label: World Heritage
mw.text: Malawi has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Lake Malawi National Park and Chongoni Rock-Art Area.

mw.label: Highest point
mw.text: The highest point in Malawi is Sapitwa (Mount Mlanje), at 3,002 m.

my.label: Name origin
my.text: Devised in the early 19th century by British geographers; the suffix -sia was added to the name of the Malay people to form a classical-style name; the name Malay may come from the Tamil word malai, meaning "mountain".

my.label: National anthem
my.text: The national anthem of Malaysia is "Negaraku" (My Country). Full version only performed in the king's presence, the shorter version performed for the queen and lesser officials.

my.label: National symbol
my.text: Malaysia's national symbols are the tiger and hibiscus.

my.label: Independence
my.text: Malaysia became independent from the UK on 31 August 1957.

my.label: World Heritage
my.text: Malaysia has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Gunung Mulu National Park and Kinabalu Park.

my.label: Highest point
my.text: The highest point in Malaysia is Gunung Kinabalu, at 4,095 m.

mv.label: Name origin
mv.text: The origin of the name is obscure but may derive from the Sanskrit word maladvipa, meaning "garland of islands;" the local name, Dhivehi Raajje, means "land of the Dhivehi people" in the local language.

mv.label: National anthem
