mv.text: The national anthem of the Maldives is "Gaumee Salaam" (National Salute). The anthem has seven verses, but only the first two are commonly used.

mv.label: National symbol
mv.text: The Maldives' national symbols are the coconut palm and yellowfin tuna.

mv.label: Independence
mv.text: The Maldives became independent from the UK on 26 July 1965.

mv.label: Highest point
mv.text: The highest point in the Maldives is 8th tee, golf course, Villingi Island, at 5 m.

mv.label: Population
mv.text: About 389,000 people live in the Maldives.

ml.label: Name origin
ml.text: Name derives from the Mali Empire of the 13th to 16th centuries A.D.

ml.label: National anthem
ml.text: The national anthem of Mali is "Le Mali" (Mali).

ml.label: National symbol
ml.text: Mali's national symbol is the Great Mosque of Djenne.

ml.label: Independence
ml.text: Mali became independent from France on 22 September 1960.

ml.label: World Heritage
ml.text: Mali has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Old Towns of Djenné and Timbuktu.

ml.label: Highest point
ml.text: The highest point in Mali is Hombori Tondo, at 1,155 m.

mt.label: Name origin
mt.text: The origin is unclear; the name may come from the ancient term mel, meaning "high" and probably referring to the island's rocks.

mt.label: National anthem
mt.text: The national anthem of Malta is "L-Innu Malti" (The Hymn of Malta). Written in the form of a prayer to bind together the political parties and the country.

mt.label: National symbol
mt.text: Malta's national symbol is the Maltese eight-pointed cross.

mt.label: Independence
mt.text: Malta became independent from the UK on 21 September 1964.

mt.label: World Heritage
mt.text: Malta has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including City of Valletta and Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum.

mt.label: Highest point
mt.text: The highest point in Malta is Ta'Dmejrek on Dingli Cliffs, at 253 m.

mh.label: Name origin
mh.text: Named after British Captain John Marshall, who charted many of the islands in 1788.

mh.label: National anthem
mh.text: The national anthem of the Marshall Islands is "Forever Marshall Islands". Words and music written by the first president of the Marshall Islands.

mh.label: National symbol
mh.text: The Marshall Islands' national symbol is the a 24-rayed star.

mh.label: Independence
mh.text: The Marshall Islands became independent from the US-administered UN trusteeship on 21 October 1986.

mh.label: World Heritage
mh.text: The Marshall Islands has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Bikini Atoll Nuclear Test Site.

mh.label: Highest point
mh.text: The highest point in the Marshall Islands is East-central Airik Island, Maloelap Atoll, at 14 m.

mr.label: Name origin
mr.text: Named for the ancient kingdom of Mauretania (3rd century B.C. to 1st century A.D.); its name derives from the Mauri (Moors) of northwest Africa.

mr.label: National anthem
mr.text: The national anthem of Mauritania is "National Anthem of Mauritania".

mr.label: National symbol
mr.text: Mauritania's national symbol is the five-pointed star between the horns of a horizontal crescent moon.

mr.label: Independence
mr.text: Mauritania became independent from France on 28 November 1960.

mr.label: World Heritage
mr.text: Mauritania has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ancient Ksour (Fortified Villages) of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt, and Oualata and Banc d'Arguin National Park.

mr.label: Highest point
mr.text: The highest point in Mauritania is Kediet Ijill, at 915 m.

mu.label: Name origin
mu.text: Named after Prince Maurice VAN Nassau, stadtholder (governor) of the Dutch Republic, in 1598.

mu.label: National anthem
mu.text: The national anthem of Mauritius is "Motherland".

mu.label: National symbol
mu.text: Mauritius' national symbols are the dodo bird and earring tree flower (Trochetia boutoniana).

mu.label: Independence
mu.text: Mauritius became independent from the UK on 12 March 1968.

mu.label: World Heritage
mu.text: Mauritius has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Aapravasi Ghat and Le Morne Cultural Landscape.

mu.label: Highest point
mu.text: The highest point in Mauritius is Mont Piton, at 828 m.

mx.label: Name origin
mx.text: Name may derive from one of the Nahuatl (Aztec) names for the capital city, Metztlixihtlico, which probably meant "the center of the moon;" alternatively, it may come from Mexica, the original name of the Aztec people.

mx.label: National anthem
mx.text: The national anthem of Mexico is "Himno Nacional Mexicano" (National Anthem of Mexico).

mx.label: National symbol
mx.text: Mexico's national symbols are the golden eagle and dahlia.

mx.label: World Heritage
mx.text: Mexico has 36 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Mexico City and Earliest 16th-Century Monasteries on the Slopes of Popocatepetl.

mx.label: Highest point
mx.text: The highest point in Mexico is Volcan Pico de Orizaba, at 5,636 m.

mx.label: Population
mx.text: About 131 million people live in Mexico.

fm.label: Name origin
fm.text: The name is a 19th-century construct of two Greek words, mikros (small) and nesoi (islands), and refers to its thousands of small islands in the western Pacific Ocean.

fm.label: National anthem
fm.text: The national anthem of Micronesia is "Patriots of Micronesia".

fm.label: National symbol
fm.text: Micronesia's national symbols are the four five-pointed white stars on a light blue field and hibiscus flower.

fm.label: Independence
fm.text: Micronesia became independent from the US-administered UN trusteeship on 3 November 1986.

fm.label: World Heritage
fm.text: Micronesia has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Center of Eastern Micronesia.

fm.label: Highest point
fm.text: The highest point in Micronesia is Nanlaud on Pohnpei, at 782 m.

md.label: Name origin
md.text: Named for the Moldova River in neighboring eastern Romania; the river's name probably comes from the Indoeuropean root word mel, meaning "dark" or "black".

md.label: National anthem
md.text: The national anthem of Moldova is "Limba noastra" (Our Tongue). Originally a 12-verse poem, but only stanzas 1, 2, 5, 9, and 12 are included in the anthem.

md.label: National symbol
md.text: Moldova's national symbol is the aurochs (type of wild cattle).

md.label: Independence
md.text: Moldova became independent from the Soviet Union on 27 August 1991.

md.label: World Heritage
md.text: Moldova has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Struve Geodetic Arc.

md.label: Highest point
md.text: The highest point in Moldova is Dealul Balanesti, at 430 m.

mc.label: Name origin
mc.text: Founded as a Greek colony in the 6th century B.C., the name's origin is unclear; it could derive from the Greek term monoikos (solitary), the Ligurian word monegu (rock), or the Basque word muno (mountain).

mc.label: National anthem
mc.text: The national anthem of Monaco is "A Marcia de Muneghu" (The March of Monaco). Only the Monegasque lyrics are official.

mc.label: National symbol
mc.text: Monaco's national symbol is the red and white lozenges (diamond shapes).

mc.label: Highest point
mc.text: The highest point in Monaco is Chemin des Revoires on Mont Agel, at 162 m.

mc.label: Capital
mc.text: The capital of Monaco is Monaco.

mn.label: Name origin
mn.text: Name comes from the Mongol people, whose name derives from the Mongol root word mengu or mongu, meaning "brave" or "unconquered;" the Mongolian name Mongol Uls translates as "Mongol State".

mn.label: National anthem
mn.text: The national anthem of Mongolia is "Mongol ulsyn toriin duulal" (National Anthem of Mongolia).

mn.label: National symbol
mn.text: Mongolia's national symbol is the Soyombo character (from the Soyombo writing system).

mn.label: World Heritage
mn.text: Mongolia has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Uvs Nuur Basin and Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape.

mn.label: Highest point
mn.text: The highest point in Mongolia is Nayramadlin Orgil (Khuiten Peak), at 4,374 m.

mn.label: Population
mn.text: About 3.3 million people live in Mongolia.

me.label: Name origin
me.text: The name in Italian means "dark mountain" and is a translation of the Serbo-Croatian name Crna Gora; both refer to the dark coniferous forests in the mountainous region.

me.label: National anthem
me.text: The national anthem of Montenegro is "Oj, svijetla majska zoro" (Oh, Bright Dawn of May).

me.label: National symbol
me.text: Montenegro's national symbol is the double-headed eagle.

me.label: World Heritage
me.text: Montenegro has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor and Durmitor National Park.

me.label: Highest point
me.text: The highest point in Montenegro is Zia Kolata, at 2,534 m.

ma.label: Name origin
ma.text: The English name of Morocco derives from, respectively, the Spanish and Portuguese names Marruecos and Marrocos, which stem from Marrakesh, the Latin name for the former capital of ancient Morocco.

ma.label: National anthem
ma.text: The national anthem of Morocco is "Hymne Cherifien" (Hymn of the Sharif).

ma.label: National symbol
ma.text: Morocco's national symbols are the pentacle symbol and lion.

ma.label: Independence
ma.text: Morocco became independent from France on 2 March 1956.

ma.label: World Heritage
ma.text: Morocco has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Medina of Fez and Medina of Marrakesh.

ma.label: Highest point
ma.text: The highest point in Morocco is Jebel Toubkal, at 4,165 m.

mz.label: Name origin
mz.text: Named for an offshore island; the island was named after Mussa bin Bique (or Mussa Ibn Malik), an influential Arab slave trader who set himself up as sultan on the island in the 15th century.

mz.label: National anthem
mz.text: The national anthem of Mozambique is “Pátria Amada” (Lovely Fatherland). The new anthem reflects the new multi-party political system.

mz.label: National symbol
mz.text: Mozambique's national symbols are the rifle, hoe and and book.

mz.label: Independence
mz.text: Mozambique became independent from Portugal on 25 June 1975.

mz.label: World Heritage
mz.text: Mozambique has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Island of Mozambique.

mz.label: Highest point
mz.text: The highest point in Mozambique is Monte Binga, at 2,436 m.

mm.label: Name origin
mm.text: Both "Burma" and "Myanmar" derive from the name of the majority Burman (Bamar) ethnic group, with the term myanma, or "the strong," being the group's name for itself.

mm.label: National anthem
mm.text: The national anthem of Myanmar is "Kaba Ma Kyei" (Till the End of the World).

mm.label: National symbol
mm.text: Myanmar's national symbol is the chinthe (mythical lion).

mm.label: Independence
mm.text: Myanmar became independent from the UK on 4 January 1948.

mm.label: World Heritage
mm.text: Myanmar has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Pyu Ancient Cities and Bagan.

mm.label: Highest point
mm.text: The highest point in Myanmar is Gamlang Razi, at 5,870 m.

na.label: Name origin
na.text: Named for the coastal Namib Desert; the word namib comes from the local Nama language and means "an area where there is nothing".

na.label: National anthem
na.text: The national anthem of Namibia is "Namibia, Land of the Brave".

na.label: National symbol
na.text: Namibia's national symbol is the oryx (antelope).

na.label: Independence
na.text: Namibia became independent from South African mandate on 21 March 1990.

na.label: World Heritage
na.text: Namibia has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Twyfelfontein or /Ui-//aes and Namib Sand Sea.

na.label: Highest point
na.text: The highest point in Namibia is Konigstein on Brandberg, at 2,573 m.

nr.label: Name origin
nr.text: The island name may derive from the Nauruan word "anaoero" meaning "I go to the beach"; the former name, Pleasant Island, came from British navigator John Frean, who visited in 1798.

nr.label: National anthem
nr.text: The national anthem of Nauru is "Nauru Bwiema" (Nauru, Our Homeland).

nr.label: National symbol
nr.text: Nauru's national symbols are the frigatebird and calophyllum flower.

nr.label: Independence
nr.text: Nauru became independent from the Australia-, NZ-, and UK-administered UN trusteeship on 31 January 1968.

nr.label: Highest point
nr.text: The highest point in Nauru is Command Ridge, at 70 m.

np.label: Name origin
np.text: The name probably comes from the Sanskrit term nepala, from the words for "fly down" and "house," which would refer to the villages at the base of the mountains.

np.label: National anthem
np.text: The national anthem of Nepal is "Sayaun Thunga Phool Ka" (Hundreds of Flowers).

np.label: National symbol
np.text: Nepal's national symbol is the rhododendron blossom.

np.label: World Heritage
np.text: Nepal has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Kathmandu Valley and Sagarmatha National Park.

np.label: Highest point
np.text: The highest point in Nepal is Mount Everest (highest peak in Asia and highest point on earth above sea level), at 8,849 m.

np.label: Population
np.text: About 31 million people live in Nepal.

nl.label: Name origin
nl.text: The English name is derived from the country's Dutch name, which means "the lowlands" and describes the geographic area; only about half the Netherlands is more than 1 meter (3.3 ft) above sea level.

nl.label: National anthem
nl.text: The national anthem of the Netherlands is "Het Wilhelmus" (The William).

nl.label: National symbol
nl.text: The Netherlands' national symbols are the lion and daisy.

nl.label: World Heritage
nl.text: The Netherlands has 13 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Schokland and Surroundings and Dutch Water Defense Lines.

nl.label: Highest point
nl.text: The highest point in the Netherlands is Mount Scenery (on the island of Saba in the Caribbean, now considered an integral part of the Netherlands following the dissolution of the Netherlands Antilles), at 862 m.

nl.label: Population
nl.text: About 18 million people live in the Netherlands.

nz.label: Name origin
nz.text: The name is an anglicized form of the Dutch name Nieuw Zeeland, or "New Sea Land," which was first used in 1643 in honor of the Dutch province of Zeeland.

nz.label: National anthem
nz.text: The national anthem of New Zealand is "God Save the King". Royal anthem and one of two official national anthems.

nz.label: National symbol
nz.text: New Zealand's national symbols are the Southern Cross constellation (four five-pointed stars), kiwi (bird) and silver fern.

nz.label: Independence
nz.text: New Zealand became independent from the UK on 26 September 1907.

nz.label: World Heritage
nz.text: New Zealand has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Te Wahipounamu – South West New Zealand and Tongariro National Park.

nz.label: Highest point
nz.text: The highest point in New Zealand is Aoraki/Mount Cook 3,724 m; note - the mountain's height was 3,764 m until 14 December 1991 when it lost about 10 m in an avalanche of rock and ice.

ni.label: Name origin
ni.text: 16th-century Spanish explorer Gil Gonzalez Davila is said to have combined the name of a local chieftain, Nicarao, with the Spanish word agua (water), referring to the two large lakes in the west of the country (Lake Managua and Lake…

ni.label: National anthem
ni.text: The national anthem of Nicaragua is "Salve a ti, Nicaragua" (Hail to Thee, Nicaragua).

ni.label: National symbol
ni.text: Nicaragua's national symbol is the turquoise-browed motmot (bird).

ni.label: Independence
ni.text: Nicaragua became independent from Spain on 15 September 1821.

ni.label: World Heritage
ni.text: Nicaragua has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ruins of León Viejo and León Cathedral.

ni.label: Highest point
ni.text: The highest point in Nicaragua is Mogoton, at 2,085 m.

ne.label: Name origin
ne.text: Named for the Niger River that passes through the southwest of the country; the name of the river probably comes from the local Tuareg name, egereou n-igereouen (big rivers).

ne.label: National anthem
ne.text: The national anthem of Niger is "L'Honneur de la Patrie" (The Honor of the Fatherland). Replaced previous national anthem, "La Nigérienne" (The Nigerien), that was adopted in 1961.

ne.label: National symbol
ne.text: Niger's national symbol is the zebu.

ne.label: Independence
ne.text: Niger became independent from France on 3 August 1960.

ne.label: World Heritage
ne.text: Niger has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Air and Ténéré Natural Reserves and W-Arly-Pendjari Complex.

ne.label: Highest point
ne.text: The highest point in Niger is Idoukal-n-Taghes, at 2,022 m.

ng.label: Name origin
ng.text: Named for the Niger River that flows through the west of the country to the Atlantic Ocean; the name of the river probably comes from the local Tuareg name, egereou n-igereouen (big rivers).

ng.label: National anthem
ng.text: The national anthem of Nigeria is "Nigeria, We Hail Thee".

ng.label: National symbol
ng.text: Nigeria's national symbol is the eagle.

ng.label: Independence
ng.text: Nigeria became independent from the UK on 1 October 1960.

ng.label: World Heritage
ng.text: Nigeria has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Sukur Cultural Landscape and Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove.

ng.label: Highest point
ng.text: The highest point in Nigeria is Chappal Waddi, at 2,419 m.

kp.label: Name origin
kp.text: Derived from the Chinese name for Goryeo, which was the Korean dynasty that united the peninsula in the 10th century A.D.; the North Korean name "Choson" means "[Land of the] Morning Calm".

kp.label: National anthem
kp.text: The national anthem of North Korea is "Aegukka" (Patriotic Song). North Korea's and South Korea's anthems have the same name and a similar melody, but different lyrics.

kp.label: National symbol
kp.text: North Korea's national symbols are the red star and chollima (winged horse).

kp.label: Independence
kp.text: North Korea became independent from Japan on 15 August 1945.

kp.label: World Heritage
kp.text: North Korea has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Koguryo Tombs Complex and Historic Monuments and Sites in Kaesong.

kp.label: Highest point
kp.text: The highest point in North Korea is Paektu-san, at 2,744 m.

mk.label: Name origin
mk.text: The name derives from the ancient kingdom of Macedon (7th to 2nd centuries B.C.), whose name origin is unclear; it may derive from the mythological Macedon, the son of the Greek god Zeus.

mk.label: National anthem
mk.text: The national anthem of North Macedonia is "Denes nad Makedonija" (Today Over Macedonia). Written in 1943 and adopted in 1991, the song previously served as the anthem of the Socialist Republic of Macedonia, when it was part of Yugoslavia.

mk.label: National symbol
mk.text: North Macedonia's national symbol is the eight-rayed sun.

mk.label: World Heritage
mk.text: North Macedonia has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Natural and Cultural Heritage of the Ohrid Region and Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians.

mk.label: Highest point
mk.text: The highest point in North Macedonia is Golem Korab (Maja e Korabit), at 2,764 m.

mk.label: Population
mk.text: About 2.1 million people live in North Macedonia.

no.label: Name origin
no.text: Derives from the Old Norse words norre and vegr, meaning "northern way," and refers to the long coastline of western Norway.

no.label: National anthem
no.text: The national anthem of Norway is "Kongesangen" (Song of the King). Royal anthem.

no.label: National symbol
no.text: Norway's national symbol is the lion.

no.label: World Heritage
no.text: Norway has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Bryggen and Urnes Stave Church.

no.label: Highest point
no.text: The highest point in Norway is Galdhopiggen, at 2,469 m.

no.label: Population
no.text: About 5.5 million people live in Norway.

om.label: Name origin
om.text: The origin of the name is uncertain, but it may date back at least 2,000 years, with an "Omana" mentioned by Pliny the Elder (1st century A.D.) and an "Omanon" by Ptolemy (2nd century A.D.).

om.label: National anthem
om.text: The national anthem of Oman is "Nashid as-Salaam as-Sultani" (The Sultan's Anthem). New lyrics written after Qaboos bin Said al Said came to power in 1970.

om.label: National symbol
om.text: Oman's national symbol is the khanjar dagger on top of two crossed swords.

om.label: World Heritage
om.text: Oman has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Bahla Fort and Archaeological Sites of Bat.

om.label: Highest point
om.text: The highest point in Oman is Jabal Shams, at 3,004 m.

om.label: Population
om.text: About 4 million people live in Oman.

pk.label: Name origin
pk.text: The name is said to have been proposed in the early 1930s by Muslim students at Cambridge University, created from the initials of Punjab, Afghanistan, and Kashmir.

pk.label: National anthem
pk.text: The national anthem of Pakistan is "Qaumi Tarana" (National Anthem). Also known as "Pak sarzamin shad bad" (Blessed Be the Sacred Land).

pk.label: National symbol
pk.text: Pakistan's national symbols are the five-pointed star between the horns of a waxing crescent moon and jasmine.

pk.label: Independence
pk.text: Pakistan became independent from British India on 14 August 1947.

pk.label: World Heritage
pk.text: Pakistan has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Archaeological Ruins at Moenjodaro and Buddhist Ruins of Takht-i-Bahi.

pk.label: Highest point
pk.text: The highest point in Pakistan is K2 (Mt. Godwin-Austen), at 8,611 m.

pw.label: Name origin
pw.text: From the Palauan name for the islands, Belau, which likely derives from the Palauan word beluu, meaning "village".

pw.label: National anthem
pw.text: The national anthem of Palau is "Belau rekid" (Our Palau).

pw.label: National symbol
pw.text: Palau's national symbol is the bai (native meeting house).

pw.label: Independence
pw.text: Palau became independent from the US-administered UN trusteeship on 1 October 1994.

pw.label: World Heritage
pw.text: Palau has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Rock Islands Southern Lagoon.

pw.label: Highest point
pw.text: The highest point in Palau is Mount Ngerchelchuus, at 242 m.

pa.label: Name origin
pa.text: Origin is unclear; may come from a Guarani word meaning "place of many fish".

pa.label: National anthem
pa.text: The national anthem of Panama is "Himno Istmeno" (Isthmus Hymn).

pa.label: National symbol
pa.text: Panama's national symbol is the harpy eagle.

pa.label: World Heritage
pa.text: Panama has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Caribbean Fortifications and Darien National Park.

pa.label: Highest point
pa.text: The highest point in Panama is Volcan Baru, at 3,475 m.

pa.label: Population
pa.text: About 4.5 million people live in Panama.

pg.label: Name origin
pg.text: The name derives from the Malay word pua-pua, describing the tightly curled hair of the Papuan people.

pg.label: National anthem
pg.text: The national anthem of Papua New Guinea is "O Arise, All You Sons".

pg.label: National symbol
pg.text: Papua New Guinea's national symbol is the bird of paradise.

pg.label: Independence
pg.text: Papua New Guinea became independent from the Australia-administered UN trusteeship on 16 September 1975.

pg.label: World Heritage
pg.text: Papua New Guinea has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Kuk Early Agricultural Site.

pg.label: Highest point
pg.text: The highest point in Papua New Guinea is Mount Wilhelm, at 4,509 m.

py.label: Name origin
py.text: Derives from the river of the same name; the river's name may come from the Guarani words para (water or river) and guay (born).

py.label: National anthem
py.text: The national anthem of Paraguay is "Paraguayos, Republica o muerte!" (Paraguayans, the Republic or Death!).

py.label: National symbol
py.text: Paraguay's national symbol is the lion.

py.label: World Heritage
py.text: Paraguay has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad de Paraná and Jesús de Tavarangue.

py.label: Highest point
py.text: The highest point in Paraguay is Cerro Pero, at 842 m.

py.label: Population
py.text: About 7.6 million people live in Paraguay.

pe.label: Name origin
pe.text: The name may derive from the Guarani word biru, meaning "river".

pe.label: National anthem
pe.text: The national anthem of Peru is "Himno Nacional del Peru" (National Anthem of Peru).

pe.label: National symbol
pe.text: Peru's national symbol is the vicuna (a camelid related to the llama).

pe.label: Independence
pe.text: Peru became independent from Spain on 28 July 1821.

pe.label: World Heritage
pe.text: Peru has 13 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Cuzco and Machu Picchu.

pe.label: Highest point
pe.text: The highest point in Peru is Nevado Huascaran, at 6,746 m.

ph.label: Name origin
ph.text: Named in honor of King Phillip II of Spain by Spanish explorer Ruy Lopez de Villalobos, who visited the islands in 1543.

ph.label: National anthem
ph.text: The national anthem of the Philippines is "Lupang Hinirang" (Chosen Land). Only sung in Tagalog.

ph.label: National symbol
ph.text: The Philippines' national symbols are the three stars and sun and Philippine eagle.

ph.label: Independence
ph.text: The Philippines became independent from the US on 4 July 1946.

ph.label: World Heritage
ph.text: The Philippines has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Baroque Churches of the Philippines and Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park.

ph.label: Highest point
ph.text: The highest point in the Philippines is Mount Apo, at 2,954 m.

pl.label: Name origin
pl.text: The name probably comes from the Slavic word pole (field or plain), indicating the flat nature of the country.

pl.label: National anthem
pl.text: The national anthem of Poland is "Mazurek Dabrowskiego" (Dabrowski's Mazurka).

pl.label: National symbol
pl.text: Poland's national symbol is the white crowned eagle.

pl.label: World Heritage
pl.text: Poland has 17 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Krakow and Historic Warsaw.

pl.label: Highest point
pl.text: The highest point in Poland is Rysy, at 2,499 m.

pl.label: Population
pl.text: About 39 million people live in Poland.

pt.label: Name origin
pt.text: Name derives from the Roman designation "Portus Cale," meaning "Port of Cale;" Cale was located in present-day northern Portugal, and its name is said to come from the Latin word calere (to be warm) because the harbor never iced over.

pt.label: National anthem
pt.text: The national anthem of Portugal is "A Portugesa" (The Song of the Portuguese). Originally written to protest the Portuguese monarchy's acquiescence to the 1890 British ultimatum forcing Portugal to give up areas of Africa.

pt.label: National symbol
pt.text: Portugal's national symbol is the armillary sphere (a spherical astrolabe for modeling objects in the sky).

pt.label: World Heritage
pt.text: Portugal has 17 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Évora and Central Zone of the Town of Angra do Heroismo in the Azores.

pt.label: Highest point
pt.text: The highest point in Portugal is Ponta do Pico (Pico or Pico Alto) on Ilha do Pico in the Azores, at 2,351 m.

pt.label: Population
pt.text: About 10 million people live in Portugal.

qa.label: Name origin
qa.text: The name may derive from the Arabic word katran, meaning "tar" or "resin" in reference to the area's oil and natural gas reserves.

qa.label: National anthem
qa.text: The national anthem of Qatar is "Al-Salam Al-Amiri" (Peace be to the Emir).

qa.label: National symbol
qa.text: Qatar's national symbol is the a white serrated band with nine white points on top of a maroon field.

qa.label: Independence
qa.text: Qatar became independent from the UK on 3 September 1971.

qa.label: World Heritage
qa.text: Qatar has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Al Zubarah Archaeological Site.

qa.label: Highest point
qa.text: The highest point in Qatar is Tuwayyir al Hamir, at 103 m.

ro.label: Name origin
ro.text: The name derives from the Latin Romani, meaning "people from Rome;" the area was an outpost of the Roman Empire in the 2nd century A.D., and the current name was adopted when Moldavia and Wallachia merged in 1861.

ro.label: National anthem
ro.text: The national anthem of Romania is "Desteapta-te romane!" (Wake up, Romanian!). The anthem was written during the 1848 Revolution.

ro.label: National symbol
ro.text: Romania's national symbol is the golden eagle.

ro.label: World Heritage
ro.text: Romania has 11 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Danube Delta and Churches of Moldavia.

ro.label: Highest point
ro.text: The highest point in Romania is Moldoveanu, at 2,544 m.

ro.label: Population
ro.text: About 18 million people live in Romania.

ru.label: Name origin
ru.text: Russian lands were referred to as Muscovy until Peter I declared the Empire of All Russias in 1721; the new name aimed at identifying the new Russia with European political tradition.

ru.label: National anthem
ru.text: The national anthem of Russia is “Gosudarstvenny Gimn Rossiyskoy Federatsii” (National Anthem of the Russian Federation). Russia adopted the tune of the Soviet Union's anthem (composed in 1939), as well as new lyrics.

ru.label: National symbol
ru.text: Russia's national symbols are the bear and double-headed eagle.

ru.label: World Heritage
ru.text: Russia has 33 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Centre of Saint Petersburg and Related Groups of Monuments and Kizhi Pogost.

ru.label: Highest point
ru.text: The highest point in Russia is Gora El'brus (highest point in Europe), at 5,642 m.

ru.label: Population
ru.text: About 140 million people live in Russia.

rw.label: Name origin
rw.text: The country is named for a local people, but the meaning of their own name is obscure.

rw.label: National anthem
rw.text: The national anthem of Rwanda is "Rwanda nziza" (Rwanda, Our Beautiful Country).

rw.label: National symbol
rw.text: Rwanda's national symbol is the traditional woven basket with peaked lid.

rw.label: Independence
rw.text: Rwanda became independent from Belgium-administered UN trusteeship on 1 July 1962.

rw.label: World Heritage
rw.text: Rwanda has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Memorial sites of the Genocide: Nyamata, Murambi, Gisozi and Bisesero and Nyungwe National Park.

rw.label: Highest point
rw.text: The highest point in Rwanda is Volcan Karisimbi, at 4,519 m.

kn.label: Name origin
kn.text: Explorer Christopher Columbus visited the islands in 1493 and named one for his own patron saint; a common nickname for Christopher during the following centuries was Kit or Kitt, and Saint Kitts is still referred to as Saint Christopher.

kn.label: National anthem
kn.text: The national anthem of Saint Kitts and Nevis is "God Save the King". In use since 1745.

kn.label: National symbol
kn.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis' national symbols are the brown pelican and royal poinciana (flamboyant) tree.

kn.label: Independence
kn.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis became independent from the UK on 19 September 1983.

kn.label: World Heritage
kn.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park.

kn.label: Highest point
kn.text: The highest point in Saint Kitts and Nevis is Mount Liamuiga, at 1,156 m.

lc.label: Name origin
lc.text: Believed to be named after Saint Lucy (Sainte Alousie) of Syracuse by French sailors who were shipwrecked on the island on 13 December 1502, the saint's feast day.

lc.label: National anthem
lc.text: The national anthem of Saint Lucia is "God Save the King". In use since 1745.

lc.label: National symbol
lc.text: Saint Lucia's national symbols are the twin pitons (volcanic peaks) and Saint Lucia parrot.

lc.label: Independence
lc.text: Saint Lucia became independent from the UK on 22 February 1979.

lc.label: World Heritage
lc.text: Saint Lucia has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Pitons Management Area.

lc.label: Highest point
lc.text: The highest point in Saint Lucia is Mount Gimie, at 948 m.

vc.label: Name origin
vc.text: Explorer Christopher Columbus named the island after Saint Vincent of Saragossa because 22 January 1498, the day of discovery, was the saint's feast day.

vc.label: National anthem
vc.text: The national anthem of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is "God Save the King". In use since 1745.

vc.label: National symbol
vc.text: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' national symbol is the Saint Vincent parrot.

vc.label: Independence
vc.text: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines became independent from the UK on 27 October 1979.

vc.label: Highest point
vc.text: The highest point in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is La Soufriere, at 1,234 m.

vc.label: Population
vc.text: About 101,000 people live in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

ws.label: Name origin
ws.text: The name's meaning and origin are unclear; some assert that it can mean "place of the moa bird" of Polynesian mythology, or it could be a local chieftain's name.

ws.label: National anthem
ws.text: The national anthem of Samoa is "O le Fu'a o le Sa'olotoga o Samoa" (The Banner of Freedom). Also known as "Samoa Tula'i" (Samoa Arise).

ws.label: National symbol
ws.text: Samoa's national symbol is the Southern Cross constellation (five five-pointed stars).

ws.label: Independence
ws.text: Samoa became independent from New Zealand-administered UN trusteeship on 1 January 1962.

ws.label: Highest point
ws.text: The highest point in Samoa is Mount Silisili, at 1,857 m.

sm.label: Name origin
sm.text: Named after Saint Marinus, who founded a monastic settlement on Monte Titano in the early 4th century.

sm.label: National anthem
sm.text: The national anthem of San Marino is "Inno Nazionale della Repubblica" (National Anthem of the Republic). The music for the anthem, which has no lyrics, is based on a 10th-century chorale piece.

sm.label: National symbol
sm.text: San Marino's national symbols are the three peaks and each displaying a tower.

sm.label: World Heritage
sm.text: San Marino has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: San Marino Historic Center and Mount Titano.

sm.label: Highest point
sm.text: The highest point in San Marino is Monte Titano, at 739 m.

sm.label: Population
sm.text: About 35,000 people live in San Marino.

st.label: Name origin
st.text: Sao Tome was named after Saint Thomas the Apostle by the Portuguese who discovered the island on 21 December 1470 (or 1471), the saint's feast day.

st.label: National anthem
st.text: The national anthem of São Tomé and Príncipe is "Independencia total" (Total Independence).

st.label: National symbol
st.text: São Tomé and Príncipe's national symbol is the palm tree.

st.label: Independence
st.text: São Tomé and Príncipe became independent from Portugal on 12 July 1975.

st.label: Highest point
st.text: The highest point in São Tomé and Príncipe is Pico de Sao Tome, at 2,024 m.

st.label: Population
st.text: About 224,000 people live in São Tomé and Príncipe.

sa.label: Name origin
sa.text: Named after the ruling dynasty of the country, the House of Saud; the name Arabia can be traced back at least as far as the ancient Romans, who referred to the peninsula as "Arabia Felix" (Arabia the Fortunate).

sa.label: National anthem
sa.text: The national anthem of Saudi Arabia is "Aash Al Maleek" (Long Live Our Beloved King).

sa.label: National symbol
sa.text: Saudi Arabia's national symbol is the palm tree over two crossed swords.

sa.label: World Heritage
sa.text: Saudi Arabia has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Hegra Archaeological Site (al-Hijr / Madā ͐ in Ṣāliḥ) and At-Turaif District in ad-Dir'iyah.

sa.label: Highest point
sa.text: The highest point in Saudi Arabia is As Sarawat range,, at 3,000 m.

sa.label: Population
sa.text: About 37 million people live in Saudi Arabia.

sn.label: Name origin
sn.text: Named for the Senegal River that forms the northern border of the country.

sn.label: National anthem
sn.text: The national anthem of Senegal is "Pincez tous vos koras, frappez les balafons" (Pluck Your Koras, Strike the Balafons).

sn.label: National symbol
sn.text: Senegal's national symbol is the lion.

sn.label: World Heritage
sn.text: Senegal has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Island of Gorée and Niokolo-Koba National Park.

sn.label: Highest point
sn.text: The highest point in Senegal is unnamed elevation 2.8 km southeast of Nepen Diaka, at 648 m.

sn.label: Population
sn.text: About 19 million people live in Senegal.

rs.label: Name origin
rs.text: The country takes its name from the Serb people; the origin of their name is unclear but may derive from the Caucasian root word ser, meaning "man".

rs.label: National anthem
rs.text: The national anthem of Serbia is "Boze pravde" (God of Justice). Song originally written as part of a play in 1872, and the Serbian people have used it as an anthem in the 20th and 21st centuries.

rs.label: National symbol
rs.text: Serbia's national symbol is the white double-headed eagle.

rs.label: World Heritage
rs.text: Serbia has 4 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Stari Ras and Sopoćani and Studenica Monastery.

rs.label: Highest point
rs.text: The highest point in Serbia is Midzor, at 2,169 m.

rs.label: Population
rs.text: About 6.7 million people live in Serbia.

sc.label: Name origin
sc.text: Named by French Captain Corneille Nicholas Morphey after Jean Moreau de Séchelles, the finance minister of France, in 1756; the British changed the spelling of the name in 1815 when they acquired the islands.

sc.label: National anthem
sc.text: The national anthem of Seychelles is "Koste Seselwa" (Seychellois Unite).

sc.label: National symbol
sc.text: Seychelles' national symbol is the coco de mer (sea coconut).

sc.label: Independence
sc.text: Seychelles became independent from the UK on 29 June 1976.

sc.label: World Heritage
sc.text: Seychelles has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Aldabra Atoll and Vallée de Mai Nature Reserve.

sc.label: Highest point
sc.text: The highest point in Seychelles is Morne Seychellois, at 905 m.

sl.label: Name origin
sl.text: Portuguese explorer Pedro de Sintra is usually credited with naming the country "Serra da Leao" (Lion Mountains) in 1462, but Venetian explorer Alvise CA' DA Mosto recorded the name as "Serre-Lionne" in 1457, referring to the rumbling of…

sl.label: National anthem
sl.text: The national anthem of Sierra Leone is "High We Exalt Thee, Realm of the Free".

sl.label: National symbol
sl.text: Sierra Leone's national symbol is the lion.

sl.label: Independence
sl.text: Sierra Leone became independent from the UK on 27 April 1961.

sl.label: World Heritage
sl.text: Sierra Leone has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Gola-Tiwai Complex.

sl.label: Highest point
sl.text: The highest point in Sierra Leone is Loma Mansa (Bintimani), at 1,948 m.

sg.label: Name origin
sg.text: Name derives from the Sanskrit words simha (lion) and pur (city); according to Malayan folklore, an Indian prince visited Singapore in the 7th century and mistook the first animal he saw for a lion, which is not native to the country.

sg.label: National anthem
sg.text: The national anthem of Singapore is "Majulah Singapura" (Onward, Singapore). The anthem is sung only in Malay.

sg.label: National symbol
sg.text: Singapore's national symbols are the lion, merlion (mythical half-lion, half-fish creature) and orchid.

sg.label: Independence
sg.text: Singapore became independent from Malaysian Federation on 9 August 1965.

sg.label: World Heritage
sg.text: Singapore has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Singapore Botanic Gardens.

sg.label: Highest point
sg.text: The highest point in Singapore is Bukit Timah, at 166 m.

sk.label: Name origin
sk.text: The country takes its name from the local Slav ethnic group; the origin of the group's name is unclear, although early forms were used in Medieval Latin (Sclavus) and Byzantine Greek (Sklabos).

sk.label: National anthem
sk.text: The national anthem of Slovakia is "Nad Tatrou sa blyska" (Storm Over the Tatras).

sk.label: National symbol
sk.text: Slovakia's national symbol is the double-barred cross (Cross of St. Cyril and St. Methodius) over three peaks.

sk.label: World Heritage
sk.text: Slovakia has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Town of Banská Štiavnica and Levoča, Spišský Hrad, and the Associated Cultural Monuments.

sk.label: Highest point
sk.text: The highest point in Slovakia is Gerlachovsky Stit, at 2,655 m.

sk.label: Population
sk.text: About 5.6 million people live in Slovakia.

si.label: Name origin
si.text: The country's name means "Land of the Slavs" in Slovene; the origin of the Slav name is unclear, although early forms were used in Medieval Latin (Sclavus) and Byzantine Greek (Sklabos).

si.label: National anthem
si.text: The national anthem of Slovenia is "Zdravljica" (A Toast). Originally written in 1848.

si.label: National symbol
si.text: Slovenia's national symbol is the Mount Triglav.

si.label: Independence
si.text: Slovenia became independent from Yugoslavia on 25 June 1991.

si.label: World Heritage
si.text: Slovenia has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Škocjan Caves and Ancient and Primeval Beech Forests of the Carpathians and Other Regions of Europe.

si.label: Highest point
si.text: The highest point in Slovenia is Triglav, at 2,864 m.

sb.label: Name origin
sb.text: Spanish explorer Alvaro de Mendana named the isles in 1568 after the wealthy biblical King Solomon in the mistaken belief that the islands contained great riches.

sb.label: National anthem
sb.text: The national anthem of the Solomon Islands is "God Save the King". In use since 1745.

sb.label: Independence
sb.text: The Solomon Islands became independent from the UK on 7 July 1978.

sb.label: World Heritage
sb.text: The Solomon Islands has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: East Rennell.

sb.label: Highest point
sb.text: The highest point in the Solomon Islands is Mount Popomanaseu, at 2,335 m.

sb.label: Population
sb.text: About 739,000 people live in the Solomon Islands.

so.label: Name origin
so.text: The name means "Land of the Somali," a local ethnic group; the origin of the group's name is unclear but may come from 1) a Cushitic word meaning "dark," 2) the local phrase soo mal, meaning "go and milk" (referring to offering guests…

so.label: National anthem
so.text: The national anthem of Somalia is "Qolobaa Calankeed" (Every Nation Has Its Own Flag).

so.label: National symbol
so.text: Somalia's national symbol is the leopard.

so.label: Independence
so.text: Somalia became independent from a merger of British Somaliland, which became independent from the UK on 26 June 1960, and Italian Somaliland, which became independent from the Italian-administered UN trusteeship on 1 July 1960 to form the…

so.label: Highest point
so.text: The highest point in Somalia is Mount Shimbiris, at 2,460 m.

so.label: Population
so.text: About 20 million people live in Somalia.

za.label: Name origin
za.text: Self-descriptive name from the country's location on the continent.

za.label: National anthem
za.text: The national anthem of South Africa is "National Anthem of South Africa".

za.label: National symbol
za.text: South Africa's national symbols are the springbok (antelope) and king protea flower.

za.label: World Heritage
za.text: South Africa has 12 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Fossil Hominid Sites of South Africa and iSimangaliso Wetland Park.

za.label: Highest point
za.text: The highest point in South Africa is Ntheledi (Mafadi), at 3,450 m.

za.label: Population
za.text: About 61 million people live in South Africa.

kr.label: Name origin
kr.text: Derived from the Chinese name for Goryeo, which was the Korean dynasty that united the peninsula in the 10th century A.D.

kr.label: National anthem
kr.text: The national anthem of South Korea is "Aegukga" (Patriotic Song). North Korea's and South Korea's anthems have the same name and a similar melody, but different lyrics.

kr.label: National symbol
kr.text: South Korea's national symbols are the taegeuk (yin-yang symbol), Rose of Sharon (Hibiscus syriacus) and Siberian tiger.

kr.label: Independence
kr.text: South Korea became independent from Japan on 15 August 1945.

kr.label: World Heritage
kr.text: South Korea has 17 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Jeju Volcanic Island and Lava Tubes and Changdeokgung Palace Complex.

kr.label: Highest point
kr.text: The highest point in South Korea is Halla-san, at 1,950 m.

ss.label: Name origin
ss.text: Self-descriptive name from the country's geographic position within Sudan prior to independence; the name Sudan derives from the Arabic balad-as-sudan, meaning "Land of the Black [peoples]".

ss.label: National anthem
ss.text: The national anthem of South Sudan is "South Sudan Oyee!" (South Sudan, Hooray!). Anthem selected in a national contest.

ss.label: National symbol
ss.text: South Sudan's national symbol is the African fish eagle.

ss.label: Independence
ss.text: South Sudan became independent from Sudan on 9 July 2011.

ss.label: Highest point
ss.text: The highest point in South Sudan is Kinyeti, at 3,187 m.

ss.label: Population
ss.text: About 13 million people live in South Sudan.

es.label: Name origin
es.text: Derivation of the name España is uncertain; the Basque words ezpain or espan ("edge," as in a river bank) are possible sources, or the Punic word span, meaning "rabbit;" some academics tie it to the god Hesperus from Greco-Roman mythology.

es.label: National anthem
es.text: The national anthem of Spain is "Himno Nacional Espanol" (National Anthem of Spain). The Spanish anthem was the first to be officially adopted.

es.label: National symbol
es.text: Spain's national symbol is the Pillars of Hercules.

es.label: World Heritage
es.text: Spain has 50 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Cave of Altamira and Paleolithic Cave Art of Northern Spain and Works of Antoni Gaudí.

es.label: Highest point
es.text: The highest point in Spain is Pico de Teide (Tenerife) on Canary Islands, at 3,718 m.

es.label: Population
es.text: About 47 million people live in Spain.

lk.label: Name origin
lk.text: The name is composed of the Sanskrit words shri (happiness or holiness) and lanka (island).

lk.label: National anthem
lk.text: The national anthem of Sri Lanka is "Sri Lanka Matha" (Mother Sri Lanka).

lk.label: National symbol
lk.text: Sri Lanka's national symbols are the lion and water lily.

lk.label: Independence
lk.text: Sri Lanka became independent from the UK on 4 February 1948.

lk.label: World Heritage
lk.text: Sri Lanka has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ancient City of Polonnaruwa and Ancient City of Sigiriya.

lk.label: Highest point
lk.text: The highest point in Sri Lanka is Pidurutalagala, at 2,524 m.

sd.label: Name origin
sd.text: The name derives from the Arabic balad-as-sudan, meaning "Land of the Black [peoples]".

sd.label: National anthem
sd.text: The national anthem of Sudan is "Nahnu Djundulla Djundulwatan" (We Are the Army of God and of Our Land). Originally served as the anthem of the Sudanese military.

sd.label: National symbol
sd.text: Sudan's national symbol is the secretary bird.

sd.label: Independence
sd.text: Sudan became independent from Egypt and the UK on 1 January 1956.

sd.label: World Heritage
sd.text: Sudan has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Gebel Barkal and the Sites of the Napatan Region and Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe.

sd.label: Highest point
sd.text: The highest point in Sudan is Jabal Marrah, at 3,042 m.

sr.label: Name origin
sr.text: Name may derive from the Surinen people who inhabited the area at the time of European contact.

sr.label: National anthem
sr.text: The national anthem of Suriname is "God zij met ons Suriname!" (God Be With Our Suriname). Originally adapted from a Sunday-school song written in 1893.

sr.label: National symbol
sr.text: Suriname's national symbols are the royal palm and faya lobi (flower).

sr.label: Independence
sr.text: Suriname became independent from the Netherlands on 25 November 1975.

sr.label: World Heritage
sr.text: Suriname has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Central Suriname Nature Reserve and Historic Inner City of Paramaribo.

sr.label: Highest point
sr.text: The highest point in Suriname is Juliana Top, at 1,230 m.

se.label: Name origin
se.text: Name derives from the North Germanic Svea tribe that inhabited central Sweden; the tribe's name probably comes from the Old German word sweba, meaning "independent;" the local form of the country's name, Sverige, means "kingdom of the Svea".

se.label: National anthem
se.text: The national anthem of Sweden is "Kungssangen" (Royal Song). Only the first verse is sung if the monarch is present.

se.label: National symbol
se.text: Sweden's national symbols are the three crowns and lion.

se.label: World Heritage
se.text: Sweden has 15 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Royal Domain of Drottningholm and Laponian Area.

se.label: Highest point
se.text: The highest point in Sweden is Kebnekaise South, at 2,100 m.

se.label: Population
se.text: About 11 million people live in Sweden.

ch.label: Name origin
ch.text: Name derives from the canton of Schwyz, one of the founding cantons of the Swiss Confederacy formed in the late 13th century.

ch.label: National symbol
ch.text: Switzerland's national symbol is the Swiss cross (white cross on red field).

ch.label: World Heritage
ch.text: Switzerland has 13 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Old City of Berne and Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

ch.label: Highest point
ch.text: The highest point in Switzerland is Dufourspitze on Monte Rosa, at 4,634 m.

ch.label: Population
ch.text: About 8.9 million people live in Switzerland.

ch.label: Capital
ch.text: The capital of Switzerland is Bern.

sy.label: Name origin
sy.text: The source of the name is uncertain; the name appears as "Suri" in Babylonian cuneiform writings dating from about 4000 B.C.

sy.label: National symbol
sy.text: Syria's national symbol is the northern bald ibis.

sy.label: Independence
sy.text: Syria became independent from League of Nations mandate under French administration on 17 April 1946.

sy.label: World Heritage
sy.text: Syria has 6 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ancient City of Damascus and Ancient City of Bosra.

sy.label: Highest point
sy.text: The highest point in Syria is Mount Hermon (Jabal a-Shayk), at 2,814 m.

sy.label: Population
sy.text: About 24 million people live in Syria.

tj.label: Name origin
tj.text: The Persian suffix -ostan means "land," so the country name means "Land of the Tajik [people];" the name Tajik comes from the Sanskrit tajika, a name originally used to distinguish Arabs from Turks and derived from the Tay, an Arab people.

tj.label: National anthem
tj.text: The national anthem of Tajikistan is "Surudi milli" (National Anthem). After the fall of the Soviet Union, Tajikistan kept the music of its Soviet-era anthem, but adopted new lyrics.

tj.label: National symbol
tj.text: Tajikistan's national symbols are the arc of seven five-pointed stars over a crown and Marco Polo sheep.

tj.label: Independence
tj.text: Tajikistan became independent from the Soviet Union on 9 September 1991.

tj.label: World Heritage
tj.text: Tajikistan has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Proto-urban Site of Sarazm and Tajik National Park (Mountains of the Pamirs).

tj.label: Highest point
tj.text: The highest point in Tajikistan is Qullai Somoniyon, at 7,495 m.

tz.label: Name origin
tz.text: The country's name is a combination of the first letters of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, the two states that merged to form Tanzania in 1964.

tz.label: National anthem
tz.text: The national anthem of Tanzania is "Mungu ibariki Afrika" (God Bless Africa). The anthem, which is also a popular African popular song in Africa, shares the melody of Zambia's anthem and is part of South Africa's anthem.

tz.label: National symbol
tz.text: Tanzania's national symbols are the Uhuru (freedom) torch and giraffe.

tz.label: World Heritage
tz.text: Tanzania has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara.

tz.label: Highest point
tz.text: The highest point in Tanzania is Kilimanjaro (highest point in Africa), at 5,895 m.

tz.label: Population
tz.text: About 69 million people live in Tanzania.

th.label: Name origin
th.text: The name means "Land of the Thai," referring to the local population; the people's name comes from the Thai word tha, meaning "to be free;" the former name of Siam comes from the Sanskrit word syama, meaning "dark".

th.label: National anthem
th.text: The national anthem of Thailand is "Phleng Sanlasoen Phra Barami" (A Salute to the Monarch). Royal anthem, played in the presence of the royal family and during certain state ceremonies.

th.label: National symbol
th.text: Thailand's national symbols are the garuda (mythical half-man, half-bird figure) and elephant.

th.label: World Heritage
th.text: Thailand has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic City of Ayutthaya and Historic Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns.

th.label: Highest point
th.text: The highest point in Thailand is Doi Inthanon, at 2,565 m.

th.label: Population
th.text: About 70 million people live in Thailand.

tl.label: Name origin
tl.text: The name partly derives from the Indonesian and Malay word timur, meaning "east;" leste is the Portuguese word for "east," so "Timor-Leste" literally means "Eastern-East".

tl.label: National anthem
tl.text: The national anthem of Timor-Leste is "Patria" (Fatherland). The song was first used as an anthem when Timor-Leste declared its independence from Portugal in 1975.

tl.label: National symbol
tl.text: Timor-Leste's national symbol is the Mount Ramelau.

tl.label: Highest point
tl.text: The highest point in Timor-Leste is Foho Tatamailau, at 2,963 m.

tl.label: Population
tl.text: About 1.4 million people live in Timor-Leste.

tl.label: Capital
tl.text: The capital of Timor-Leste is Dili.

tg.label: Name origin
tg.text: The name derives from the town of Togodo (now Togoville) on the northern shore of Lake Togo; the town's name probably comes from the lake's name, which is composed of the Ewe words to ("water") and go ("shore").

tg.label: National anthem
tg.text: The national anthem of Togo is "Salut à toi, pays de nos aieux" (Hail to Thee, Land of Our Forefathers). Anthem was replaced during one-party rule between 1979 and 1992.

tg.label: National symbol
tg.text: Togo's national symbol is the lion.

tg.label: Independence
tg.text: Togo became independent from French-administered UN trusteeship on 27 April 1960.

tg.label: World Heritage
tg.text: Togo has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Koutammakou.

tg.label: Highest point
tg.text: The highest point in Togo is Mont Agou, at 986 m.

to.label: Name origin
to.text: The name is of local origin and is said to mean "island;" the former name, the Friendly Islands, came from Captain James Cook in 1773, based on the welcome he received from the inhabitants.

to.label: National anthem
to.text: The national anthem of Tonga is "Ko e fasi 'o e tu'i 'o e 'Otu Tonga" (Song of the King of the Tonga Islands). In use since 1874.

to.label: National symbol
to.text: Tonga's national symbol is the red cross on white field.

to.label: Independence
to.text: Tonga became independent from UK protectorate status on 4 June 1970.

to.label: Highest point
to.text: The highest point in Tonga is Kao Volcano on Kao Island, at 1,046 m.

tt.label: Name origin
tt.text: Explorer Christopher Columbus named the larger island "La Isla de la Trinidad" (The Island of the Trinity) in 1498, possibly because of the three mountain peaks on the island.

tt.label: National anthem
tt.text: The national anthem of Trinidad and Tobago is "Forged From the Love of Liberty". Song originally written as an anthem for the West Indies Federation.

tt.label: National symbol
tt.text: Trinidad and Tobago's national symbols are the scarlet ibis (bird of Trinidad), cocrico (bird of Tobago) and chaconia flower.

tt.label: Independence
tt.text: Trinidad and Tobago became independent from the UK on 31 August 1962.

tt.label: Highest point
tt.text: The highest point in Trinidad and Tobago is El Cerro del Aripo, at 940 m.

tt.label: Population
tt.text: About 1.4 million people live in Trinidad and Tobago.

tn.label: Name origin
tn.text: The country name derives from the capital city of Tunis.

tn.label: National anthem
tn.text: The national anthem of Tunisia is "Humat Al Hima" (Defenders of the Homeland). Mohamad Abdel Wahab also composed the music for the anthem of the United Arab Emirates.

tn.label: National symbol
tn.text: Tunisia's national symbol is the red crescent moon and five-pointed star in a white circle.

tn.label: Independence
tn.text: Tunisia became independent from France on 20 March 1956.

tn.label: World Heritage
tn.text: Tunisia has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Amphitheatre of El Jem and Archaeological Site of Carthage.

tn.label: Highest point
tn.text: The highest point in Tunisia is Jebel ech Chambi, at 1,544 m.

tr.label: Name origin
tr.text: The name means "Land of the Turks".

tr.label: National anthem
tr.text: The national anthem of Türkiye is "Istiklal Marsi" (The March of Independence). The anthem's original music was adopted in 1924.

tr.label: National symbol
tr.text: Türkiye's national symbol is the vertical crescent moon with adjacent five-pointed star.

tr.label: World Heritage
tr.text: Türkiye has 22 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Archaeological Site of Troy and Ephesus.

tr.label: Highest point
tr.text: The highest point in Türkiye is Mount Ararat, at 5,137 m.

tr.label: Population
tr.text: About 85 million people live in Türkiye.

tm.label: Name origin
tm.text: The suffix -stan means "land," so the country name means the "Land of the Turkmen [people];" the people's name means "Turk-like," from the Persian words tork and mandan, referring to their formerly nomadic lifestyle that differed from the…

tm.label: National anthem
tm.text: The national anthem of Turkmenistan is "Garaşsyz, Bitarap Türkmenistanyň" (Independent, Neutral, Turkmenistan State Anthem).

tm.label: National symbol
tm.text: Turkmenistan's national symbol is the Akhal-Teke horse.

tm.label: Independence
tm.text: Turkmenistan became independent from the Soviet Union on 27 October 1991.

tm.label: World Heritage
tm.text: Turkmenistan has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Ancient Merv and Kunya-Urgench.

tm.label: Highest point
tm.text: The highest point in Turkmenistan is Gora Ayribaba, at 3,139 m.

tv.label: Name origin
tv.text: The name in the local language means "group of eight" or "eight standing together," referring to eight of the country's nine islands.

tv.label: National anthem
tv.text: The national anthem of Tuvalu is "God Save the King". Used since 1745.

tv.label: National symbol
tv.text: Tuvalu's national symbol is the maneapa (native meeting house).

tv.label: Independence
tv.text: Tuvalu became independent from the UK on 1 October 1978.

tv.label: Highest point
tv.text: The highest point in Tuvalu is unnamed location, at 5 m.

ug.label: Name origin
ug.text: The name is derived from the Swahili word u, meaning "land" or "country," and the Ganda people; the origin of the Ganda name is unclear.

ug.label: National anthem
ug.text: The national anthem of Uganda is "O Uganda, Land of Beauty!". One of the shortest national anthems in the world.

ug.label: National symbol
ug.text: Uganda's national symbol is the grey crowned crane.

ug.label: Independence
ug.text: Uganda became independent from the UK on 9 October 1962.

ug.label: World Heritage
ug.text: Uganda has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Bwindi Impenetrable National Park and Rwenzori Mountains National Park.

ug.label: Highest point
ug.text: The highest point in Uganda is Margherita Peak on Mount Stanley, at 5,110 m.

ua.label: Name origin
ua.text: The name derives from the Old East Slavic or Old Russian word ukraina, meaning "borderland," which was used to describe the area on medieval Russia's border at the time of the Tatar invasion in the 13th century.

ua.label: National anthem
ua.text: The national anthem of Ukraine is "Shche ne vmerla Ukraina" (Ukraine Has Not Yet Perished). Current version of the anthem is the first verse of Chubynskyi's poem, plus the chorus.

ua.label: National symbol
ua.text: Ukraine's national symbols are the tryzub (trident) and sunflower.

ua.label: World Heritage
ua.text: Ukraine has 8 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Kyiv: Saint Sophia Cathedral and Related Monastic Buildings, Kyiv Pechersk Lavra and Lviv Historic Center.

ua.label: Highest point
ua.text: The highest point in Ukraine is Hora Hoverla, at 2,061 m.

ua.label: Population
ua.text: About 36 million people live in Ukraine.

ae.label: National anthem
ae.text: The national anthem of the United Arab Emirates is "Nashid al-watani al-imarati" (National Anthem of the UAE). Mohamad Abdel Wahab also composed the music for Tunisia's and Libya's anthem.

ae.label: National symbol
ae.text: The United Arab Emirates' national symbol is the golden falcon.

ae.label: Independence
ae.text: The United Arab Emirates became independent from the UK on 2 December 1971.

ae.label: World Heritage
ae.text: The United Arab Emirates has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Cultural Sites of Al Ain (Hafit, Hili, Bidaa Bint Saud, and Oases Areas) and Faya Palaeolandscape.

ae.label: Highest point
ae.text: The highest point in the United Arab Emirates is Jabal Bil 'Ays, at 1,905 m.

gb.label: Name origin
gb.text: The name United Kingdom is self-descriptive; the name Britain probably derives from the Celtic word pretani, meaning "painted people;" the designation of Great Britain for England, Scotland, and Wales dates back to medieval times and was…

gb.label: National anthem
gb.text: The national anthem of the United Kingdom is "God Save the King". In use since 1745.

gb.label: World Heritage
gb.text: The United Kingdom has 33 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Giant's Causeway and Causeway Coast and Ironbridge Gorge.

gb.label: Highest point
gb.text: The highest point in the United Kingdom is Ben Nevis, at 1,345 m.

gb.label: Population
gb.text: About 69 million people live in the United Kingdom.

gb.label: Capital
gb.text: The capital of the United Kingdom is London.

us.label: Name origin
us.text: The name America was first used in 1507 and is derived from the first name of Amerigo Vespucci (1454-1512), an Italian explorer, navigator, and cartographer.

us.label: National anthem
us.text: The national anthem of the United States is "The Star-Spangled Banner".

us.label: National symbol
us.text: The United States' national symbol is the bald eagle.

us.label: World Heritage
us.text: The United States has 26 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Yellowstone National Park and Grand Canyon National Park.

us.label: Population
us.text: About 338 million people live in the United States.

us.label: Capital
us.text: The capital of the United States is Washington D.C..

uy.label: Name origin
uy.text: Name derives from the Uruguay River, which makes up the western border of the country; the river's name comes from the Guarani words uru (bird) and guay (tail).

uy.label: National anthem
uy.text: The national anthem of Uruguay is "Himno Nacional" (National Anthem of Uruguay). The anthem is also known as "Orientales, la Patria o la tumba!" ("Uruguayans, the Fatherland or Death!").

uy.label: National symbol
uy.text: Uruguay's national symbol is the Sun of May (a sun-with-face symbol).

uy.label: Independence
uy.text: Uruguay became independent from Brazil on 25 August 1825.

uy.label: World Heritage
uy.text: Uruguay has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic City of Colonia del Sacramento and Fray Bentos Industrial Landscape.

uy.label: Highest point
uy.text: The highest point in Uruguay is Cerro Catedral, at 514 m.

uz.label: Name origin
uz.text: The name comes from the local people, the Uzbeks, whose name is said to have originated with Mongol leader Ghiyath ad-Din Muhammad Uzbek; the Persian suffix -stan means "country".

uz.label: National anthem
uz.text: The national anthem of Uzbekistan is "O'zbekiston Respublikasining Davlat Madhiyasi" (National Anthem of the Republic of Uzbekistan).

uz.label: National symbol
uz.text: Uzbekistan's national symbol is the khumo (mythical bird).

uz.label: Independence
uz.text: Uzbekistan became independent from the Soviet Union on 1 September 1991.

uz.label: World Heritage
uz.text: Uzbekistan has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Itchan Kala and Historic Bukhara.

uz.label: Highest point
uz.text: The highest point in Uzbekistan is Xazrat Sulton Tog', at 4,643 m.

vu.label: Name origin
vu.text: The name means "Our land forever" in several of the Austronesian languages spoken on the islands.

vu.label: National anthem
vu.text: The national anthem of Vanuatu is "Yumi, Yumi, Yumi" (We, We, We). The anthem is written in the native Bislama.

vu.label: National symbol
vu.text: Vanuatu's national symbol is the boar's tusk with crossed fern fronds.

vu.label: Independence
vu.text: Vanuatu became independent from France and the UK on 30 July 1980.

vu.label: World Heritage
vu.text: Vanuatu has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Chief Roi Mata’s Domain.

vu.label: Highest point
vu.text: The highest point in Vanuatu is Tabwemasana, at 1,877 m.

va.label: Name origin
va.text: "holy" comes from the Greek word hera, meaning "sacred"; "see" comes from the Latin word sedes, meaning "seat," and refers to the episcopal chair.

va.label: National symbol
va.text: The Vatican City's national symbol is the crossed keys under a papal tiara.

va.label: World Heritage
va.text: The Vatican City has 2 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Historic Center of Rome, the Properties of the Holy See in that City Enjoying Extraterritorial Rights and San Paolo Fuori le Mura and Vatican City.

va.label: Highest point
va.text: The highest point in the Vatican City is Vatican Gardens (Vatican Hill), at 78 m.

va.label: Population
va.text: About 1,000 people live in the Vatican City.

va.label: Capital
va.text: The capital of the Vatican City is Vatican City.

ve.label: Name origin
ve.text: In 1499, the stilt-houses built on Lake Maracaibo reminded explorers Alonso de Ojeda and Amerigo Vespucci of buildings in Venice, Italy, and they named the region "Venezuola," meaning "Little Venice".

ve.label: National anthem
ve.text: The national anthem of Venezuela is "Gloria al bravo pueblo" (Glory to the Brave People). Both Salias and Landaeta were executed in 1814 during Venezuela's fight for independence.

ve.label: National symbol
ve.text: Venezuela's national symbol is the troupial (bird).

ve.label: Independence
ve.text: Venezuela became independent from Spain on 5 July 1811.

ve.label: World Heritage
ve.text: Venezuela has 3 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Coro and its Port and Canaima National Park.

ve.label: Highest point
ve.text: The highest point in Venezuela is Pico Bolivar, at 4,978 m.

vn.label: Name origin
vn.text: The name translates as "Viet south;" Viet is an ethnic term of unknown origin that dates back to ancient times, and nam (south) refers to the country's location.

vn.label: National anthem
vn.text: The national anthem of Vietnam is "Tien quan ca" (The Song of the Marching Troops). It became the national anthem of the unified Socialist Republic of Vietnam in 1976.

vn.label: National symbol
vn.text: Vietnam's national symbols are the five-pointed yellow star on a red field and lotus blossom.

vn.label: Independence
vn.text: Vietnam became independent from France on 2 September 1945.

vn.label: World Heritage
vn.text: Vietnam has 9 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Complex of Hué Monuments and Ha Long Bay.

vn.label: Highest point
vn.text: The highest point in Vietnam is Fan Si Pan, at 3,144 m.

ye.label: Name origin
ye.text: The name origin is unclear but may come from the Arabic word al-yamin, meaning "the right," as a reference to its geographic position in relation to Mecca.

ye.label: National anthem
ye.text: The national anthem of Yemen is "Al-qumhuriyatu l-muttahida" (United Republic). The music first served as the anthem for South Yemen before unification with North Yemen in 1990.

ye.label: National symbol
ye.text: Yemen's national symbol is the golden eagle.

ye.label: World Heritage
ye.text: Yemen has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Old Walled City of Shibam and Old City of Sana'a.

ye.label: Highest point
ye.text: The highest point in Yemen is Jabal an Nabi Shu'ayb, at 3,666 m.

ye.label: Population
ye.text: About 35 million people live in Yemen.

zm.label: Name origin
zm.text: Name is derived from the Zambezi River, which flows through the western part of the country and forms the southern border with Zimbabwe.

zm.label: National anthem
zm.text: The national anthem of Zambia is "Lumbanyeni Zambia" (Stand and Sing of Zambia, Proud and Free). The melody, which comes from the popular song "God Bless Africa," a popular song and anthem in southern Africa.

zm.label: National symbol
zm.text: Zambia's national symbol is the African fish eagle.

zm.label: Independence
zm.text: Zambia became independent from the UK on 24 October 1964.

zm.label: World Heritage
zm.text: Zambia has one UNESCO World Heritage Site: Mosi-oa-Tunya/Victoria Falls.

zm.label: Highest point
zm.text: The highest point in Zambia is Mafinga Central, at 2,330 m.

zw.label: Name origin
zw.text: Takes its name from the Kingdom of Zimbabwe (13th-15th century) and its capital of Great Zimbabwe, which was built of stone.

zw.label: National anthem
zw.text: The national anthem of Zimbabwe is "Kalibusiswe Ilizwe leZimbabwe" [Ndebele] "Simudzai Mureza WeZimbabwe" [Shona] (Blessed Be the Land of Zimbabwe).

zw.label: National symbol
zw.text: Zimbabwe's national symbols are the Zimbabwe bird symbol, African fish eagle and flame lily.

zw.label: Independence
zw.text: Zimbabwe became independent from the UK on 18 April 1980.

zw.label: World Heritage
zw.text: Zimbabwe has 5 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including Mana Pools National Park, Sapi, and Chewore Safari Areas and Great Zimbabwe National Monument.

zw.label: Highest point
zw.text: The highest point in Zimbabwe is Inyangani, at 2,592 m.
